This is the boldest idea here and the one with the most evidence behind it. I'd build the site around this one. Recruiters and friends drop in their own photo and watch my PictoTrack logic run: EXIF block, DMS→decimal, hemisphere flip, plus a real Otsu threshold and dilation bitmaps. It all happens on-device, with zero uploads, and it's honestly labelled as a re-implementation. That proves a project that has no repo link, without touching the empty links placeholder. Add #12's offline dotted-map pin.

The gate itself, though, adds 4–5 pins, about 3.5 viewports of held scroll, and it duplicates #19's opener ceremony. Take the foundations now and leave the pin out.

Eyecatch cards are a real anime convention. Falling through a summoning ring into the next series' colours, with both palettes meeting on the rim (gate-d-50.png), is original and very much mine. It also deletes both tickers, which were lifted from CarbonZero, and adds per-section data-palette scoping, which fixes headings arriving in the previous anime's colours. Keep the budgets short. Five pins on top of the other choreography would tire recruiters out.

tally.title: Through the Sigil: the first scroll flies you through the ManaCore

But it rewrites ManaCore, which #0 deletes, pins the hero for about 60 svh before any real content, and collides with #33 and #24, which also rework the hero. Scaling the 437 px SVG by 7x on phones risks blurry or oversized layers. Only do it after the hero stack (#33, #24, #0 phase 1) settles, and rebuild it on whichever renderer survives.

Flying through the hollow centre of the circle you just watched being cast and coming out in Black Clover crimson is a jaw-drop moment. It's written against ManaCore.tsx, which #0 deletes, and it's the same boundary as the first gate in #6. Build it as the GPU stage's hero→Work transition (and that gate) instead of a separate three.js camera rig.

tally.title: The cast becomes the scene: one continuous GPU shot from preloader to hero
reasons: An intro that becomes the page rather than cutting to it is a jury-pleasing move, and the hard 0.85 s fallback to SVG is a responsible design. It depends entirely on #0 and should merge with #8: the GL particles carry the sigil, and the DOM FLIP carries the name, the kanji and 剣/杖.

The intro circle's particles become the hero sigil in one unbroken shot, with no crossfade between two renderers. That's the first five seconds I'd show a friend. It only works once #0 exists, and the 0.85 s fallback to the SVG keeps it safe. Build it as the sigil half of #8, not as a separate system.

tally.title: Summoned plates: each character art plate is cut out by a shader and materialises through a different spell per series
reasons: The problem is real: stack.webp, path.webp and contact.webp sit on light grounds and look pasted on. But a chroma-key on studio anime art will halo hair, especially on SAO's streaked sky. Five different dissolves turn the plates into an effects reel. #20 solves the same problem honestly and holds up better. Keep the shader matte only as a possible future fallback.

It solves a real measured problem (border luma of 225/208/187 on the stack, contact and path plates) the hard way. The DOM images go to opacity 0 and are redrawn as scissored GL views that must stay pixel-locked to scroll, with five bespoke dissolve shaders and a chroma key the proposer admits will halo the SAO sky. If GL stalls, the art disappears. #20 fixes the same plates in pure CSS, and plate-test.png option C already looks right.

observations: three.js is used only by ManaCore (src/components/ui/ManaCore.tsx), which draws LineLoop, LineSegments and Points and nothing else. In the current build it costs two lazy chunks: .next/static/chunks/b536a0f1.*.js is 323,064 B raw / 75,260 B gzip and bd904a5c.*.js is 175,803 B / 46,724 B. That is about 122 kB gzip for one hero ornament. Phones never load it because of the `wide` gate in src/components/sections/Hero.tsx; they get the SVG MagicCircle at 50% opacity instead (mob-hero.png).

ManaCore's own comments say every WebGL line is 1px and that 'density is the only way to get visual weight'. There is no bloom. Once settled, the sigil is a crisp but thin dotted disc (design/webgl/desk-hero-7s.png). It also sits behind the right-hand intro paragraph at x≈736–1100 (desk-hero.png), which hurts legibility. An IntersectionObserver stops it after the hero, so the scene ends at the fold.

There are five independent rAF loops: SmoothScroll (Lenis), ManaCore, FlowField (a 2D canvas with up to 900 per-particle strokes), Petals (a full-viewport 2D canvas at z-[1], running on phones too) and framer-motion. The Lenis instance is private to SmoothScroll.tsx, although Lenis 1.1.20 exposes velocity and direction (node_modules/lenis/dist/lenis.d.ts:266-276). Nothing can react to scroll speed today.

Section backgrounds are opaque color-mix washes (.motif-field and #work in src/app/globals.css; at runtime they compute to color(srgb .05 .097 .099)). Any persistent backdrop canvas needs an html.gl override that makes them transparent, with the wash painted on the GPU instead. Hero.tsx's -z-10 layers sit in the root stacking context because the hero section is not `isolate`, so a stage canvas must go at z -20.
The `.noise` grain is a fixed full-viewport div at z 9998 with mix-blend-mode: soft-light (globals.css). It blends the whole page every time anything repaints.

Three of the five owner-supplied plates have light backgrounds. Mean border luma: stack.webp 225, contact.webp 208, path.webp 187 (work 16, about 45). On the dark default they show as bright feathered rectangles (design/webgl/desk-stack.png, desk-contact.png; contact sheet at design/webgl/plates.png). They are RGB webp with no alpha, so only a shader matte can cut the characters out.

ProjectArtwork.tsx is a placeholder by its own comment ('Swap this component for <Image /> once real screenshots exist'). The CarbonZero card is concentric SVG rings and PictoTrack is SVG bars (desk-work.png), and hover adds a MagicCircle SVG overlay.

The preloader (src/components/layout/Preloader.tsx) is SVG plus framer. Its departure tilts and fades the SVG while the hero's ManaCore is a separate drawing, so the 'handoff' is really a crossfade between two renderers. Its geometry (C=200, R_GLYPH=150, 48 RUNES, TRIANGLES) is in the file and can be reused directly.

CarbonZero reference: its GPU work is one dotted, glowing globe pinned to the hero (cz/main-0.png, cz/cz-1800.png). Prototype built and rendered: design/webgl/proto/stage.html, raw WebGL2 with no library. It has 24,576 motes, seven formations baked into an RGBA32F texture read with texelFetch(gl_VertexID), a staggered curl-noise morph, a 5-level dual-Kawase bloom, velocity chromatic aberration plus a vertical streak, grain, vignette and the GPU section wash. Output: proto-f0.png (hero floor sigil), proto-f1.png (grimoire), proto-f2.png (bolt), proto-sheet.png (wand/sword, aperture, bloom, and the bolt at velocity 0.9), proto-t15.png (mid-morph swarm). Every formation reads clearly.

Prototype cost: 19.3 kB raw source, 7.0 kB gzip, and 6.1 kB gzip with comments stripped, before any minification. That covers all formation generators and every pass, against 122 kB gzip for three.js today.

Prototype speed on the same CPU rasteriser (SwiftShader), so the figures are relative only: 104 ms/frame at 1440×900 and 52 ms at 390×844 with the full bloom chain. The live site's hero (ManaCore + FlowField + Petals) measured 7.3 fps, about 136 ms/frame, on that rasteriser. The test browser reports WebGL2 with MAX_VERTEX_ATTRIBS 16 and EXT_color_buffer_float, so morph-by-texture and RGBA16F bloom targets work.

Real content counts are available to drive formations without inventing anything: timeline has 4 entries, hackathons 6 and nav 6 (src/lib/content.ts). The data-section 'hobby' has no CSS palette pair, so it inherits Path's colours.

Nothing on the page is pinned. The loader's sigil flight is hard-coded (`translateX: '29vw', translateY: '-3vh', scale: 0.46, rotateX: 56, opacity: 0`). I measured the production build in .next with my own short-lived `next start` on :3105, using Playwright and the PerformanceObserver APIs for LCP, CLS, long tasks and paint, CDP traces and metrics, a screencast filmstrip, axe-core run against each section in both themes, keyboard walks, reduced-motion and no-JS contexts. Desktop was 1440x900. Mobile was 390x844 with 4x CPU and 1.6 Mbps / 150 ms RTT. Caveat: this sandbox renders WebGL through SwiftShader, which inflates GPU-bound timings, so treat GPU-heavy numbers as relative. The CPU, hydration, LCP and a11y numbers are representative. Scripts and screenshots are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-portfolio/36b10c1b-248c-5794-91de-a620612c7efa/scratchpad/design/craft/ (perf.mjs, a11y.mjs, film.mjs, skip.mjs, stale.mjs, trace.mjs, recalc.mjs, menu.mjs, focus.mjs, reduced.mjs, a11y.json, perf-*.json, film-sheet.png, nojs-hero.png, 404.png, og.png, reduced-compare.png, contact-error-light.png).
observations: JS weight. From .next/app-build-manifest.json, the first-load JS for "/" is about 191 KB gz across the layout and page chunk graph, excluding polyfills. The 103 KB figure is only the shared part. On viewports of 768px and up, next/dynamic in src/components/sections/Hero.tsx lazily adds three.js as 2 chunks, bd904a5c (45 KB gz) and b536a0f1 (73 KB gz), so 118 KB gz. Phones never request them; I checked that 0 three chunks load at 390px.

LCP is gated by hydration (mobile, throttled, intro skipped). FCP was 1424 ms and LCP was 5404 ms. The LCP element is the hero intro

. Framer `initial` SSRs it at opacity:0, and it only becomes visible after hydration plus a 1.05 s delay (src/components/sections/Hero.tsx). On desktop with the intro skipped, LCP was 5680 ms after a 3.4 s long task at ManaCore init; SwiftShader inflates that. On a desktop first visit, LCP was 4576 ms and the element was the preloader's own wordmark. The hero h1, the biggest text on the page, never qualifies as LCP because CharReveal splits it into 15 inline-block chars (src/components/ui/TextReveal.tsx).

The site chrome flashes before the intro. In the first-visit filmstrip at 4x CPU, the nav, the telemetry strip and an empty hero are on screen from about 1.3 s to 2.85 s before the preloader mounts. The cause is in src/components/layout/Preloader.tsx: it starts with useState(true) and only sets done=false inside useEffect, so the 'cast' opens on a flash of the page it is meant to precede. While the intro plays, the second Tab press lands on 'Skip to content' behind the overlay. The overlay has role="presentation" and the page is not inert.

With no JS (or a failed bundle), the hero renders blank. 161 elements are SSR'd with inline opacity:0, the theme falls back to light because <html data-theme="light"> is the SSR default, and the stat counters read 0 / 0 yrs / 0 / 0 (src/components/ui/Counter.tsx). See nojs-hero.png.

The skip link is broken while Lenis is active. The anchor handler in src/components/providers/SmoothScroll.tsx calls preventDefault and then lenis.scrollTo, so the browser never moves the sequential focus starting point. Measured: pressing Enter on 'Skip to content' leaves focus on the link, and the next Tab goes to the nav wordmark. Pressing Enter on '04 Path' and then Tab goes to '05 Hobby'. With reduced motion (no Lenis) both behave correctly.

ARIA gaps. In src/components/sections/Skills.tsx the role="tab" buttons have no tabpanel, no aria-controls and no arrow-key handling. In src/components/layout/Nav.tsx the mobile overlay has no role or aria-modal, and #main is not inert behind it. There is no aria-current anywhere. The 剣/杖 toggle has no aria-pressed. The hero h1 depends on aria-label on a generic span, which ARIA 1.2 prohibits.

axe-core, with each section scrolled into place, both themes. The only violation is 'definition-list' (serious) on the hero stats
: dd comes before dt, and there is a

inside dl>div. Hand-measured: the contact form's error text is text-red-400 on the light-theme contact wash at about 2.2:1, which fails AA (contact-error-light.png). The fields get no aria-invalid or aria-describedby.

The petals are one anime behind. Petals.tsx and FlowField.tsx re-read --accent through MutationObserver plus getComputedStyle at the instant data-section flips, which returns the @property transition's start value. Measured paint colours: in #work the petals use 60 214 140 / 162 118 255 (the default pair, not crimson/gold). In #path they use 167 139 250 / 86 200 255 (Stack's pair). ManaCore avoids this only because it polls every 10 frames.

Reduced motion is mostly right: 0 running animations, Lenis off, and the canvases are static or removed. One gap: ManaCore renders a single frame and never re-renders, so after a theme toggle the dark-mode, additive-blended sigil sits nearly invisible on the light background (reduced-compare.png).

Motion speed depends on frame rate. ManaCore uses t = frame/60, FlowField does time += 16 and moves particles per frame, and Petals does t += 1. On 120 Hz and 144 Hz displays all ambient motion runs 2 to 2.4 times too fast.

Idle and scroll churn. There are three separate 1 Hz intervals (Nav.tsx at xl, Telemetry.tsx and Footer.tsx). At 1280px and wider, Nav and Telemetry show the same IST clock about 40px apart. Telemetry's Cell component is defined inside render, so it remounts every tick. On phones Telemetry is display:none but still calls setState on every scroll frame, and it reads 'Section 01 Work' while you are on the hero (and on the 404). On phones Petals clears and redraws a full-viewport DPR-2 canvas every frame forever, for 4 petals (min(w*h/78000,18)). An idle trace at phone size showed 10 style recalcs in 2 s touching about 7,200 elements.

Cost of the section crossfade. Each @property frame restyles about 790 of the 1,872 DOM elements: a 2 s trace showed 23 UpdateLayoutTree passes, 18,107 elements and 147 ms at 1x CPU. That is about 25 ms per frame at 4x CPU during every section boundary, plus about 27 ms of forced style flushes from the canvases' MutationObserver reads.

No error boundaries. When I aborted the three.js chunk request, the whole page was replaced by Next's 'Application error: a client-side exception has occurred'. src/app has no error.tsx or global-error.tsx, and the next/dynamic import in Hero.tsx has no catch.

The contact form reports success without delivering. With RESEND_API_KEY and CONTACT_TO_EMAIL unset, src/app/api/contact/route.ts returns {ok:true} and only calls console.info. A valid submit showed 'Thanks — I’ll be in touch shortly.' while the server logged '[contact] message received (no mail provider configured)'.

Theme and chrome mismatch. In layout.tsx, viewport.themeColor is keyed to prefers-color-scheme, but themeScript forces dark. A phone in light mode therefore gets a #f4f3ee browser bar over a #08060e page. `color-scheme` is not set anywhere, so native controls, scrollbars and autofill ignore the dark default.

Edges are generic. The OG image (src/app/opengraph-image.tsx, og.png) is plain default sans with 2 colour bars: no sigil, no section palette, no Japanese. Case studies exist only inside a modal with no URL, so nothing can be deep-linked or shared. There is no apple-icon or manifest, and the favicon is a gradient 'M'. not-found.tsx is a plain large '404' (404.png). There are no view transitions; the theme toggle swaps instantly.

Fonts are 7 files, about 253 KB. 85 KB of that is Inter latin-ext (8e9860b6e62d6359-s.woff2), downloaded only for ₹, ō, ū and Ō (src/lib/content.ts lines 384, 436, 443 and 464). The JAPAN RAMEN file is 6.9 KB and preloaded but uses display:'swap' with adjustFontFallback:false. That is harmless today because the h1 waits for hydration, but it becomes a CLS risk once the h1 paints at FCP.

Things that are already good: CLS is 0.0025 to 0.0028 (nav condense only). The case-study modal traps focus and restores it. FlowField and ManaCore pause off-screen. Phones never load three.js. The focus outline is a 2px accent ring and is visible on every control except inputs, which use an underline bar instead.

proposals.title: ManaStage: one persistent GPU sigil that changes form for each series (three.js removed)
proposals.pitch: One fixed WebGL2 canvas sits behind the whole page. In the hero, 24k mana motes form ManaCore's tilted summoning disc, now glowing instead of 1px. As each section header arrives, they stream off and reassemble around that section's character plate as a ground sigil. Work becomes a grimoire thrown open under a pentagram, About a bolt through halftone, Stack a wand and sword crossed under a star chart, Path a floating tower of floors, Hobby a six-blade camera aperture, and Contact a five-petal bloom shedding petals. Between headers the motes thin into a dim ambient field. Colours come from the same @property channels, so the swarm crossfades with the page.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero's WebGL is one globe pinned to its hero (main-0.png); after the fold it is stock photography. Here the 3D object carries the story: it lasts through all six sections, changes form per anime, and is built from the site's own SectionArt geometry. It costs about 7 kB gzip against the Three.js + react-three-fiber stack CarbonZero ships, and phones get it too, which they never did here.
proposals.approach:
Engine (src/lib/gl/engine.ts) is raw WebGL2 with no library, following design/webgl/proto/stage.html. It uses one VAO of N vec4 seeds and a formation texture (RGBA32F, 256 × N/256 × F rows; xyz = position, w = size/brightness, negative w = HUD-locked) fetched in the vertex shader with texelFetch(gl_VertexID). The morph uses uniforms uFrom/uTo/uMix. Each mote has its own stagger, t = smoothstep(clamp((mix - seed.x*.4)/.6)), plus a curl-noise detour scaled by sin(πt), so motes swarm instead of sliding in lockstep. Per-formation tilt and spin uniforms put the hero at rx(-1.15) with in-plane spin and give the tower a y-spin. Particles are drawn additively into an RGBA16F target, falling back to RGBA8 with lower gain.

Formations (src/lib/gl/formations.ts) port ManaCore's ring/ticks/dottedDisc/star generators for the hero. The others sample SectionArt.tsx's actual SVG paths with polyline, cubic and polygon samplers: the grimoire curves, the bolt polygon M238 130L150 268h62l-18 122 108-152h-66z, the sword and wand segments, the constellation, and the blossom ellipses. The Path tower has one floor per timeline entry (4) and one orbiting rune per hackathon (6), lit as each DOM row crosses the centre line. The counts are read from content.ts. The hobby aperture is new, original geometry.

Choreography (src/lib/gl/director.ts) caches doc-tops of [data-stage-anchor] elements (hero sigil box, SectionVisual slot, SectionVisualMobile, Hobby header right half) with a ResizeObserver. Each frame it picks the active anchor with the same centre-line rule as SectionTheme.tsx and sets the offset and scale from that anchor's rect, so the formation stays pixel-locked under the character.

One frame loop: src/lib/frame.ts is a ticker. SmoothScroll.tsx calls lenis.raf(t), then the subscribers, so GL never lags the DOM by a frame. Colours reuse ManaCore's readChannel on --accent/--accent-2 every 10th frame.

Legibility: up to 6 [data-stage-avoid] rects (hero intro column, section standfirsts) go in as vec4 uniforms. The composite clamps backdrop luminance inside them to ≤0.034, which keeps --muted text at ≥4.5:1 on the dark background, and to ≤0.010 behind --faint mono labels. A Playwright pixel-sampling test asserts both.

Background: under html.gl the .motif-field/#work backgrounds and their ::before washes go transparent, and the composite paints the same two radial washes, as the prototype already does. Light theme uses an 'ink' mode: normal blending, and the composite multiplies the paper colour by (1 - ink).

Mounting: src/components/gl/StageMount.tsx is 'use client' with a dynamic import (ssr:false), because layout.tsx is a server component. The canvas is fixed inset-0 -z-20, aria-hidden, pointer-events-none.

Fallbacks: no WebGL2 or a webglcontextlost event removes html.gl and brings back today's SVG MagicCircle and CSS washes. With reduced motion it renders only on scroll, resize or theme change; formations swap with a 250 ms opacity crossfade, with no swarm and no spin.
proposals.risk: This is the largest refactor of the set. GL-drawn content must stay pixel-locked to the DOM; the single ticker solves that, but iOS address-bar resizes need visualViewport handling. A formation must never sit under body text, which the avoid rects handle. Raw GL is more for a second-year student to maintain than three.js, though it is about 600 commented lines and the prototype already works. Moving petals into the Contact formation only is a taste call on the owner's 'quiet counterweight' idea. RGBA16F render targets need EXT_color_buffer_float or EXT_color_buffer_half_float; there is an RGBA8 fallback.
proposals.mobile: Phones get a GPU sigil for the first time, replacing the 50%-opacity SVG. The 'lite' tier applies below 768px or on a coarse pointer: N=8192, DPR 1, 3 bloom mips, 30 fps idle and 60 fps while scrolling. A frame-time EMA governor halves N above 20 ms and drops to render-on-scroll above 33 ms. Save-Data or deviceMemory < 4 keeps the static SVG. Formations anchor to SectionVisualMobile's in-flow plate. The added download is the roughly 7 kB engine; three.js is gone entirely.

proposals.title: Mana optics: bloom, chromatic split and speed streaks driven by scroll velocity, and computed grain
proposals.pitch: The sigil glows like light instead of hairlines. Fling the page and the backdrop smears into vertical speed lines with a red/blue split radiating from the sigil, easing out as the scroll settles. In About (My Hero Academia) the streaks run hotter; in Path (Sword Art Online) a HUD scan band and faint interlace sweep the backdrop. Text is never touched, because every effect lives only in the GL layer behind it.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero's globe has a glow, but its page is optically inert under scroll. Here scroll speed itself is visible, tuned per anime (MHA speed lines, SAO HUD scan), and the film grain is computed per frame on the GPU instead of being a blended SVG overlay.
proposals.approach:
All of this goes in the composite pass in src/lib/gl/shaders.ts, which already runs in the prototype.

Bloom: dual-Kawase over 5 mips (5-tap down, 8-tap tent up), with uBloomK 1.6 in dark. In light theme the bloom becomes an ink bleed.

Velocity: v = clamp(|lenis.velocity|/40, 0, 1), EMA-smoothed with k = .15. SmoothScroll.tsx exposes the Lenis instance through src/lib/frame.ts.

Chromatic aberration: R and B are sampled at uv ± (uv - sigilCentre) * v * .018, so the split radiates from the formation.

Streak: 6 taps along y, signed by lenis.direction and mixed by v.

Per-section multipliers:
- About: streak ×1.8. This replaces the CSS repeating-linear-gradient speed lines in globals.css.
- Path: a moving smoothstep scan band plus 1px interlace at 6%. This replaces the CSS scan-line keyframe.
- Stack: the ambient field brightens into a starfield, replacing the CSS radial-gradient stars.

Grain: hash(uv*res + frame) ±0.035, replacing the .noise overlay. There is also a vignette.

A 'Mana' FX switch (button, aria-pressed) sits next to the theme and accent toggles in Nav.tsx and is persisted by ThemeProvider as localStorage 'fx' = full|calm. Calm keeps bloom only.

With reduced motion, CA, streaks, the scan band and grain animation are hard-off; grain is static.
proposals.risk: CA and streaks can cause motion discomfort. That is mitigated by a 1.8% offset cap, a hard-off under reduced motion, and the user-facing calm switch. Additive bloom does nothing on the light theme, hence the ink-bleed variant. Fill rate on 4K and high-DPR screens is handled by running the bloom chain from a half-res scene when DPR > 1.5.
proposals.mobile: Bloom runs 3 mips at quarter resolution. CA is off by default, because touch flings produce huge velocities; streaks run at 50%; grain stays on, since it is cheaper than the current blended overlay. The calm switch is reachable in the mobile menu.

proposals.title: Summoned plates: each character art plate is cut out by a shader and materialises through a different spell per series
proposals.pitch:
The section plates are drawn by the GPU. Their flat backgrounds are keyed out, so Wistoria's pair, the SAO duo and the Fragrant Flower couple stand directly on the glowing sigil instead of inside pale rectangles. As a header scrolls in, its character materialises through a dissolve unique to the series:
- Black Clover: crimson anti-magic ash rising.
- My Hero Academia: green lightning crackle.
- Wistoria: star-dust.
- Sword Art Online: polygon shards snapping together.
- Fragrant Flower: petal-shaped bloom.

Embers from the dissolve edge fly off and join the sigil. On desktop, hovering a plate ripples it like disturbed mana.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero drops stock photos into rounded cards (main-1700.png, 'Rising temperatures' in cz-sheet.png). Here the imagery is the owner's own chosen art, integrated with the scene: cut out, lit by the section's sigil, and summoned in a way specific to each series.
proposals.approach:
The plates render as views in the same context. For each visible plate, gl.viewport and gl.scissor are set to its rect (cached offsets plus lenis.scroll) and a quad is drawn. The DOM <Image> stays for layout and as the texture source through img.currentSrc; /_next/image is same-origin, so the canvas is not tainted. Under html.gl the image gets opacity: 0.

Matte: on load, the plate is drawn into a 32×32 2D canvas and its border texels are averaged into uKey. In the shader, both go to YCbCr and matte = smoothstep(.08, .22, |CbCr - keyCbCr|*1.6 + |Y - keyY|*.6), with spill desaturation near the key and the existing FADE feather multiplied in. The fix is aimed at stack, path and contact, whose measured border luma is 225/187/208. A per-plate key flag in SectionVisual's DIMS map lets the owner opt out, for example if the streaky SAO sky halos.

Reveal: uReveal is the header's progress (0 with the plate top at 100vh, 1 at 55vh). The noise n changes per series:
- Work: fbm domain-warped upward (smoke) plus ember sparks.
- About: Voronoi F2−F1 < .05 crackle edges flickering on hash(cell, floor(t*12)).
- Stack: a 6px hash grid where each cell pops on its own beat.
- Path: skewed-grid triangle cells, each revealed at hash(id) and scaled from its centroid (SAO shatter in reverse).
- Contact: petal noise abs(sin(5·atan(p))) * r.

Then alpha = step(n, uReveal) * matte, and the edge band col += accent * 3, which the bloom picks up.

Embers: each frame the CPU emits up to 64 stage motes from edge texels of a 64×64 CPU copy of n, and they ease into the formation.

Pointer ripple (fine pointers only): uv += normalize(d) * .012 * exp(-14|d|) * sin(60|d| - 6t), with a .004 RGB split near the cursor. This is not a cursor replacement.

Textures are capped at 1024px, and only the visible plate ±1 is resident.
proposals.risk: The SAO plate's blue, streaked sky keys imperfectly and may halo hair edges, so it may need key: false. The polygon-shatter dissolve is a taste call. GL-drawn images must stay pixel-locked to scroll; the shared ticker from mana-stage covers that. Texture memory is held to about 2.5 MB per plate by the 1024px cap and lazy upload. With reduced motion the reveal is instant and the ripple is off; the matte stays, because it is a legibility fix rather than motion.
proposals.mobile: On phones the plates are already in-flow under the heading (SectionVisualMobile, 210–260px tall). Same views and same reveal, with no ripple (no hover) and embers capped at 16 per frame. The lowest tier applies the matte only.
removes: The CSS FADE mask path and opacity-[0.82] wash-out while GL is on (feathering moves into the shader)

proposals.title: Project plates that run: a GPU globe for CarbonZero and an OCR pass for PictoTrack
proposals.pitch: The two project cards stop being placeholder SVG patterns. CarbonZero's card becomes a slowly turning dotted Earth in the section's crimson and gold, a nod to the globe on CarbonZero itself, and it turns to face Kochi on hover. PictoTrack's card runs its real pipeline as a visual: a scanline sweeps a generated photo, leaving greyscale, then Otsu-thresholded, then dilated pixels behind it. Then a crosshair locks on and the DMS-to-decimal conversion types out. Open the case study and the same render grows into the modal header instead of being swapped out.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero illustrates with stock footage. Here each project's plate is a working miniature of the project: the globe CarbonZero is known for, and PictoTrack's actual OpenCV steps with a real coordinate conversion. No stock imagery and no invented figures.
proposals.approach:
Views in the shared context are scissored to each card's artwork box (the 'relative w-full overflow-hidden' div in Projects.tsx gets data-stage-view).

CarbonZero: a Fibonacci sphere of 4096 points, kept where a land mask is set. The mask is Natural Earth 1:110m land, which is public domain, rasterised offline to a 256×128 1-bit PNG (public/gl/land.png, about 3 kB). Ocean points sit at 15% alpha, with a fresnel atmosphere rim. The Kochi pin comes from site.coords (9.93°N, 76.27°E), and hover slerps the globe to face it.

PictoTrack: a procedural 256×160 plate (fbm terrain and sky plus a signboard of noise glyphs) is generated once on the CPU. JS computes a real Otsu threshold from that plate's histogram. The shader shows three bands behind the scanline (grey, binarised at the Otsu value, 3×3 max dilation), matching the OpenCV steps listed in content.ts. A DOM readout converts site.coords '09°55′N 76°16′E' to 9.9167, 76.2667 using PictoTrack's hemisphere-sign rule, labelled 'demo · this site's coordinates'.

Modal: a FLIP transition interpolates the view rect from the card to the modal header over the existing 0.55s motion.article transition, so the render is continuous. The hover MagicCircle overlay is replaced by a sigil drawn in the view.

ProjectArtwork stays as the no-GL fallback.

The land texture must be generated from public-domain vector data, not a downloaded map image. The globe could read as imitation unless it is framed as CarbonZero's own visual identity. With reduced motion, the globe holds still facing Kochi and the OCR pass shows its final frame.
proposals.mobile: The globe drops to 2048 points, auto-rotates, and settles facing Kochi when the card is centred. The OCR pass runs once per entry into view, then holds. The modal FLIP works the same on touch.

proposals.title: The cast becomes the scene: one continuous GPU shot from preloader to hero
proposals.pitch: The intro's motes, rings and hexagram are drawn by the same particles that form the hero sigil. When the name resolves, the circle is not faded out and replaced. Its particles tilt into perspective and fly into the hero's floor sigil while the page rises around them, in one unbroken shot.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero's intro (cz-top.png) is a chart that ends with 'skip intro' and a cut to its page. This intro does not end; it becomes the page. That is only possible because the engine is about 7 kB and loads before the rings land, which a 122 kB three.js chunk could not reliably do.
proposals.approach:
Preloader.tsx calls import('@/lib/gl/engine') on mount. If the engine is ready by B.rings (0.85s):
1. html.casting hides <main> (opacity 0) and the overlay background goes transparent over the stage's black clear colour.
2. The engine runs a 'scatter' → 'cast' formation built from Preloader's own constants: rings r = 188/150/96/58, the 48 RUNES, and the two TRIANGLES from vertex().
3. The existing B beat table drives uniforms. The shockwave is a radial push in the vertex shader at B.rings+0.25, and the 剣/杖 flash is a uBloomK spike at B.duality+0.55.
4. The DOM keeps the glyphs, name, Skip button and Escape handling.
5. finish() calls engine.morph('cast' → 'hero', 950ms) on the same [0.65, 0, 0.35, 1] curve the CSS departure uses, and removes html.casting so the page fades in under the moving particles.

If the engine is not ready by B.rings, today's SVG path runs unchanged. The 6.5s watchdog and the sessionStorage gate are untouched.

Optional: for the name beat, particles sample points from the wordmark rasterised client-side into a 2D canvas with the already-loaded name font, then hand off to the DOM name.
proposals.risk: The loader must never wait on GL, which the hard 0.85s cutoff to SVG guarantees. If the wordmark sampling is used, JAPAN RAMEN is a personal-use font. Rasterising it client-side on his personal site adds no new use, but it must not be baked into a shipped texture. Reduced motion is unaffected, because the preloader is already skipped there.
proposals.mobile: Same sequence on the lite tier. The cast circle is centred at min(76vmin, 620px), then flies to the hero's top-right bleed sigil. If the engine arrives late on a slow connection, the SVG intro plays exactly as it does today.
