proposals.title: Konami opens the grimoire: a live render inspector, plus a real 'MANA' cell in the telemetry strip
proposals.pitch: ↑↑↓↓←→←→BA no longer just outlines boxes. The backdrop splits into the actual render passes (scene, each bloom mip, the formation texture). The swarm is drawn as raw points with lines to their targets. A HUD lists live frame time, particle count, quality tier and pass count. The telemetry strip also gains a live MANA cell showing fps and particle count.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero's ticker streams live CO₂ data. For a developer portfolio, the honest live metric is the machine rendering it, and every number here is measured in real time, not decoration.
proposals.approach: KonamiEgg.tsx dispatches 'stage:inspect'. The engine then blits its real intermediate render targets into corner viewports with a copy program, and draws mote-to-target gl.LINES with a second program that fetches both formations. engine.stats ({ms EMA from performance.now deltas, N, tier, mips, dpr, formation, mix}) is published every 500 ms as an event. Telemetry.tsx adds a 'MANA 60fps · 24k' cell only when html.gl is set. Without GL, the existing CSS outline easter egg stays.
proposals.risk: Minimal. The pass thumbnails must stay inside the stage canvas's aria-hidden layer, and the HUD text needs AA contrast on a solid backing.
proposals.mobile: No change. The Konami code needs a keyboard, and the telemetry strip is lg-only (hidden below 1024px).
removes: Nothing; the CSS wireframe mode stays as the no-GL behaviour
proposals.lens: WebGL, shaders & 3D. One persistent GPU scene across every section, post-processing, per-series transformations of the sigil, image shaders on the art and project plates, and GPU particles. I prototyped the core and measured it, and the numbers are below.

proposals.title: Eyecatch Gates: section-to-section summoning portals
proposals.pitch: At each themed boundary the page holds for one beat, like the eyecatch card in the middle of an anime episode. On the outgoing palette, the next section's emblem and kanji light up inside a summoning ring, and '( N° 004 ) — ASCENT' decodes out of glyphs. Then the ring's interior widens into a hole and you fall through it: the new palette, character art and heading are waiting on the other side. Both series' colours meet on the ring's edge for the length of the transition.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CZ changes theme with hard cuts between dark and light bands (main-2600 light, main-4400 dark). Its one transition is a stock photo card growing to full bleed. These gates are original, aware of both palettes, built from the site's own sigil, and show two themes on screen at once, which CZ never does. They also fix the measured bug where every heading arrives in the previous section's palette.
proposals.approach: New src/components/ui/Gate.tsx, rendered at the top of each themed section (from='path' to='hobby' and so on, using the emblem, jp and index already in sectionThemes/nav). Structure: an outer spacer of height var(--gate-len) (desktop 70svh, mobile 55svh) holding a `sticky top-0 h-[100svh]` stage with `margin-bottom:-100svh`, so the stage sits over the start of its section. Drive it with framer `useScroll({target, offset:['start start','end start']})` → p, then map: ring stroke draw (pathLength) on p 0 to .35; label/kanji decode on .1 to .45; hole radius on .4 to 1, from 0 to hypot(vw,vh). The stage background is the outgoing palette wash, masked with `radial-gradient(circle at var(--ix) var(--iy), transparent var(--ir), #000 calc(var(--ir) + 1px))`, with the CSS vars written from a useMotionValueEvent. An SVG ring (rings, ticks and star generated the way MagicCircle.tsx does it) sits at the hole centre, scaled r/100 so its inner ring rides the hole's edge, rotating at p*90deg with a counter-rotating dashed ring. The hole opens from the measured position of the next header's emblem, so the portal opens where the section's mark will land. Palette scoping: duplicate the five palette blocks in globals.css as `[data-palette=x]` selectors and put data-palette on each section element. The @property channels inherit, so each subtree always shows its own colours. The gate stage carries data-palette={from}. The global data-section and its 700ms transition stay for fixed chrome (Nav, Telemetry, ManaCore, Petals). Add a palette pair for 'hobby'. Prerequisite: change overflow-hidden to overflow-x-clip on all themed sections, which also fixes the About aside. SmoothScroll's anchor handler should scroll to the section's `[data-gate-end]` so nav jumps land past the gate. Optionally, a jump across sections plays a 400ms full-screen 'teleport' version of the target gate as an overlay animation instead of a scroll. Reduced motion: a static 40svh eyecatch card (emblem, kanji, label) with no pin and no hole.
proposals.risk: Scroll fatigue: four or five pins. Mitigate with short budgets (70svh), a fast hole opening, and dropping the existing `pt-24 sm:pt-36` top padding the gate replaces; net cost is about +2.5k px on desktop after removing both tickers. mask-image repaint on very large viewports: it is one composited element, but test on a mid-range Android. The stage must be aria-hidden with pointer-events:none. When it is fully open (p=1) it reveals everything, so focus order is unaffected. Watch any z-index collision with Nav (z-9990).
proposals.mobile: Same component with a 55svh budget, a simpler ring (two circles, no ticks), and the hole opening from the emblem in the left gutter. The SectionVisualMobile plates sit under the stage and are revealed through the circle (prototype gate-m-50.png). SVG plus one CSS mask: no canvas, no three.js. Lenis does not smooth touch, so native scroll drives the sticky stage.
removes: Both <Ticker> marquee bands in src/app/page.tsx and src/components/sections/Ticker.tsx (Marquee.tsx stays; Footer uses it)
The 700ms timed palette crossfade as the only section transition (kept only for fixed chrome)

proposals.title: Through the Sigil: the first scroll flies you through the ManaCore
proposals.pitch: Your first scroll off the hero is a flythrough of the circle you just watched being cast. The name splits, MOHAMMED sliding left and MISHAL. right. The 3D sigil swings face-on and the camera dollies through its hollow centre while the motes stream past. You come out the other side in the Work section, already in Black Clover crimson.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CZ's showpiece 3D dotted globe (main-0, cz-1800) only rotates in place, and scrolling past it is an ordinary scroll. Here the 3D object is the transition: the hero's centrepiece becomes the doorway to the work.
proposals.approach: In Hero.tsx, give the hero a ~160svh scroll budget around a `sticky top-0 h-[100svh]` stage, change overflow-hidden to overflow-x-clip, and keep the existing scrollYProgress. Pass it to ManaCore as a MotionValue prop `dive`, read in the existing tick() via `dive.get()`. In ManaCore.tsx, eased d: sigil.rotation.x lerps 0.26 → ~1.27 so the disc turns face-on to the camera; the camera dollies along its view ray from (0,2.7,8.6) to just past the origin, through the empty r<0.55 core of dottedDisc; FOV widens 42 → ~70 near the pass for a brief warp; the motes group scales on z (1 → 4) so the points stretch into streaks; ring opacity drops to 0 after the pass. Each frame, project the disc centre with `new Vector3().project(camera)` and write `--iris-x/--iris-y/--iris-r` onto the hero stage. The stage's radial mask (the same technique as the gates) opens around the projected hole, so the Work section shows through the sigil's centre in the same frame the camera passes it. Projects.tsx gets a negative top margin so it sits under the hero stage. Lift ManaCore's existing radial maskImage as d → 1. Name split: add x transforms on the two h1 lines (0 → ∓60%) and open letter-spacing; the stats and status rows fade earlier. Drop the current sigilY/sigilRotate parallax. Reduced motion: the hero stays a 100svh static block, no dive.
proposals.risk: Adds about 60svh before the first real content, so keep the budget tight and make the nav's 'Work' link land past it. Warp taste: keep the pass to about 15% of progress. The canvas costs nothing extra (same draw calls); ManaCore's IntersectionObserver must keep running while the stage is pinned. Lenis inertia overshooting the pass is fine because the effect is purely position-driven.
proposals.mobile: No three.js below 768px, so this stays phone-safe. The SVG MagicCircle (already the 112vw mobile centrepiece) scales 1 → 7 and rotates 0 → 90° about its centre via useTransform, while the same CSS hole opens from its centre, giving the same choreography for almost no extra bytes. The sticky budget shrinks to 130svh.
removes: Hero sigil parallax (sigilY/sigilRotate) in Hero.tsx

proposals.title: The Cast Lands: every intro element flies to its home on the page
proposals.pitch: The intro no longer fades out; it breaks apart into the page. The six section kanji on the hexagram fly to their six nav links, which already crossfade to those same kanji on hover. 剣 and 杖 drop into the hero's duality row. The loader's wordmark rises and grows into the giant hero name. The sigil tilts and lands on the GPU ManaCore at the correct size, and the ManaCore answers with a shockwave as it ignites. Only then does the hero's own entrance play, now actually visible.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CZ's data intro (cz/*.png) ends with 'SKIP INTRO' and a cut to its landing page, and nothing from it carries over. Here everything the intro draws becomes something on the page, so the intro effectively assembles the navigation. It also fixes two measured faults: the hero entrance currently plays unseen under the loader, and the sigil lands at 0.46 scale when it needs about 1.16.
proposals.approach: New src/lib/cast.ts: setCastPhase('casting'|'departing'|'done') writes `document.documentElement.dataset.cast` and dispatches a `cast:phase` CustomEvent. New src/hooks/useCastPhase.ts uses useSyncExternalStore. In layout.tsx, extend the themeScript to set data-cast='done' before first paint when sessionStorage 'preloaded' is set or reduced motion is on, so a revisit never flashes a hidden hero. Add `data-cast-target` attributes: 'name-0'/'name-1' on the hero h1 line spans, 'sword'/'wand' on the duality glyphs, 'nav-#work' and so on on the Nav.tsx desktop links, 'burger' on the burger button, 'sigil' on the Hero sigil wrapper. In Preloader.tsx, at depart: await document.fonts.ready, measure each source/target pair, and run FLIP with framer's imperative `animate(el,{x,y,scale},{duration:.9, ease:[.65,0,.35,1], delay:i*.04})`. Split the loader wordmark into spans ('Mohammed', 'Mishal', and the trailing 'M', which fades); both ends use .wordmark/Japan Ramen, so uniform scale looks right. Fade the overlay background first so the pieces fly over the real page. Replace the hard-coded 29vw/-3vh/0.46 with the measured sigil rect at rotateX 57.7°, land at opacity 1, then crossfade over 150ms. Hero.tsx: entrance `animate` props switch to variants gated on phase !== 'casting'; CharReveal (TextReveal.tsx) gets a `play` prop; landed name lines skip CharReveal and the '.' spring-pops on arrival. ManaCore.tsx: on 'departing' plus flight time, ignite(): a ring(1,160) LineLoop scaled 0.5 → 4.2 with opacity .9 → 0 over 1.1s, a disc point-size pulse (.062 → .09 → .062), and a brief outward push on the motes. Skip/Escape go straight to 'done' with no flight; the watchdog stays.
proposals.risk: Measurement races: the Japan Ramen font swap and ManaCore's lazy chunk may not have mounted yet. Measure after fonts.ready, and fall back to the SVG MagicCircle rect, which shares the same wrapper box. Wrong targets after a resize mid-intro: re-measure at depart, not at mount. Hiding the hero until depart must never strand it, so data-cast='done' is also set by the watchdog and by skip.
proposals.mobile: Nav links are hidden below lg, so the six kanji funnel into the burger button: they scale to 0.2 and fade on contact, and the burger plays one ring pulse. The sigil lands on the 437px SVG MagicCircle at the top right instead of shrinking to 136px as it does now. The name lands on the 12.4vw h1. No three.js is involved on phones.
removes: Hard-coded departure transform in Preloader.tsx (translateX 29vw / translateY -3vh / scale .46 / opacity 0)

proposals.title: The Grimoire: Work becomes a book whose pages turn on scroll
proposals.pitch: The Work section pins and becomes an actual grimoire. Its cover, carrying the section's grimoire emblem, swings open as you scroll. Each project is a two-page spread: the generative artwork on the left page, the 'incantation' on the right (summary, catalysts, links). Keep scrolling and the page turns to PictoTrack. The last page is honestly blank, reading 'the next spell is being written', with a link to his GitHub.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CZ's pinned 'Planetary diagnostics' (main-4400.png) is a generic horizontal photo-card slide with a 01/03 counter. Here a 3D page turn driven by scroll makes the section's own metaphor literal: it is already labelled GRIMOIRE, and the case-study modal's headings are 'Incantation' and 'Catalysts'.
proposals.approach: Projects.tsx, desktop (lg) without reduced motion: a section of height calc(100svh + leaves*70svh), switched from overflow-hidden to overflow-x-clip, holding a sticky stage with `perspective:1800px`. Each leaf is a motion.div with transformOrigin 'left center', `.preserve-3d`, and rotateY = useTransform(p,[i/n,(i+1)/n],[0,-180]), with front and back faces using `.backface-hidden` (both utilities already in globals.css). A shading gradient's opacity peaks at 90° of each turn. The front of leaf i is the right page of spread i; the back is the left page of spread i+1, rendering <ProjectArtwork variant=…> with its rings and bars scrubbed by local page progress. Clicking a page opens the existing ProjectModal unchanged. An in-world 'PAGE 01 / 03' HUD readout sits in mono. Real 'Previous page' and 'Next page' buttons scroll through Lenis to each leaf's offset, with an aria-live polite announcement ('Page 2 of 3: PictoTrack'). All page content stays in DOM order. Drop Tilt inside the 3D book. The TILES bento grid remains as the mobile and reduced-motion fallback.
proposals.risk: Taste: skeuomorphism can tip into kitsch, so keep the pages flat and dark with hud-frame borders and no paper texture. Chrome can blur text mid-rotation; apply will-change only while a page is turning. About 210svh of pinned scroll for two projects. The blank final page has to read as intentional and honest, not as missing content.
proposals.mobile: No pin and no 3D. Pages sit in a native `snap-x snap-mandatory overflow-x-auto` strip you swipe to turn, with a gentle ±8° rotateY bend driven by each page's IntersectionObserver ratio. The current stacked cards also remain a valid fallback. Zero new JavaScript weight.
removes: Desktop bento TILES grid and Tilt wrapper (kept for mobile and reduced motion)

proposals.title: Kinetic Spine: scroll velocity drives the world, and labels decode
proposals.pitch: The page reacts to how you move. Fling it and the petals get swept upward in a gust, the mana field stretches into streaks, and the italic serif line of every heading leans into the motion like a speed line before springing back when you stop. Section labels and the telemetry readout decode out of katakana and sigil glyphs as they arrive. The telemetry strip gains a live VEL readout in px/s, because it is all one real signal.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: All of CZ's motion runs on time (marquees, counters, word highlight), and nothing on it notices how fast the visitor scrolls. Here every ambient system is tied to one real, measured signal, and the strip prints the number, which matches the site's rule that figures must be real.
proposals.approach: SmoothScroll.tsx: expose the Lenis instance through a React context and, in `lenis.on('scroll', ({velocity}) => …)`, write a clamped `--scroll-v` (-1..1) on <html>. New src/hooks/useScrollVelocity.ts: framer useVelocity(useScroll().scrollY) into useSpring({stiffness:400,damping:40}), normalised, used by components and as the source on touch, where Lenis does not smooth. In SectionHeader.tsx and TextReveal.tsx, line 1 (the italic serif line) gets skewX = useTransform(v,[-1,1],[8,-8]) plus a small x drift. New src/components/ui/Decode.tsx: a scramble-decode that resolves left to right over ~600ms when it comes into view. Charset: katakana plus MagicCircle's glyph band ◇✦△◯✧▽❖⬡. The real text lives in aria-label and the scrambled glyphs are aria-hidden; width is locked (mono `ch`, or a measured width) to avoid layout shift. Use it for '( N° 00X ) — LABEL' in SectionHeader and Contact, for the Telemetry SECTION cell on change, and for the gate labels. Petals.tsx and FlowField.tsx read --scroll-v in their existing CSS-var polling: petals get vy -= v*2.4 (a gust) and flow trails lengthen with |v|. Telemetry.tsx gets a 'VEL 1,240 px/s' cell from Lenis velocity × 60. ScrollProgress.tsx becomes a six-segment bar, one segment per section filling in that section's colour (an SAO-style HP bar), still driven by one motion value. Everything is gated on prefers-reduced-motion and rests at 0.
proposals.risk: Skewed italics briefly hurt readability during a fling, so cap the skew (±8° desktop, ±5° phones) and spring hard back to 0. A scramble that jitters for screen readers or shifts layout would be a regression; aria-label plus locked widths prevent both. Velocity-linked motion is a vestibular trigger, so reduced-motion parity is mandatory (Lenis is already off there, which zeroes the signal).
proposals.mobile: Velocity comes from framer's useVelocity on native touch scroll. Skew is capped lower. Petal gusts work on phones, since the canvases already run there, and decoding labels are just text. Telemetry and its VEL cell stay desktop-only (the strip is `lg:flex`). No new libraries.
removes: Plain 2px ScrollProgress hairline (replaced by the segmented section bar)

proposals.title: Four Steps, Repeated: Process as a ratcheting sigil wheel
proposals.pitch: 'Four steps, repeated' stops being a grid and becomes an actual cycle. The section pins and a large four-spoke sigil turns a quarter per step, pausing at each one: 観 Understand, 描 Sketch, 造 Build, 磨 Refine. Each kanji draws itself in at the 12 o'clock station while its description slides in alongside. The last quarter turn brings it back to 01 and the counter ticks to 'CYCLE 02', so 'repeated' is shown rather than stated.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CZ's equivalent content, 'Three steps to carbon zero' (main-3500.png), is a static three-row list with arrow buttons. Same kind of content, but here it is shown as a working mechanism, and it rescues the one band on the site with no palette and no motion.
proposals.approach: Process.tsx: add id='process' and data-palette='stack' (Wistoria's wand-and-sword cycle fits), switch to overflow-x-clip, and pin a sticky stage over a ~4×45svh budget. The wheel is an SVG generated like MagicCircle (rings, a 4-point star, four station nodes). Its rotation uses a detent mapping: useTransform(p, v => { const s=v*4, i=Math.floor(s), f=s-i; return -90*(i + easeInOutCubic(clamp((f-.35)/.3,0,1))) }), so it rests on each step and turns between them. Use a plain transform rather than a spring, since Lenis already smooths. The kanji, currently `text-accent-2/0` until hover, become each step's centrepiece: SVG <text> with a stroke-dasharray draw, then the fill fades in. Descriptions stay in a real <ol> in DOM order; the wheel is aria-hidden. Reduced motion: the existing four-column grid with the kanji always visible.
proposals.risk: This is one more pin, so ship it after gates and dive and keep the budget around 180svh. The detent mapping must feel mechanical rather than laggy. If gates, dive and grimoire all ship, check the total pinned scroll across the page for fatigue before adding this one.
proposals.mobile: No pin. The four step cards sit in a native horizontal scroll-snap carousel, with a small wheel above it rotating from the carousel's scrollLeft (framer useScroll({container})). That removes about 1,500px from the 17,021px mobile page where the cards currently stack.
removes: Process four-column hover grid on desktop (kept for reduced motion)

proposals.title: Cast it yourself: PictoTrack's EXIF route running in the page
proposals.pitch: In the PictoTrack case study, a 'Cast it yourself' panel takes a dropped or picked photo and runs PictoTrack's real fallback path in the browser. It finds the EXIF GPS block, converts the DMS rationals to decimal, flips the sign for S and W, and drops a pin on an original dotted world map. A two-node pipeline diagram (OCR, then EXIF) lights up step by step and says plainly which route this demo runs and which needs the desktop app. The photo never leaves the tab; an optional 'Look up address' button sends only the coordinates.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero is one app you visit. Here a recruiter runs a working slice of his second project inside the portfolio, built from the exact algorithm the case study describes. The dotted map answers CZ's dotted globe, but this one does a job: it plots your photo.
proposals.approach: 1) A ~90-line JPEG EXIF reader in src/lib/exif.ts: scan for APP1 'Exif\0\0', read the TIFF byte order (II/MM), walk IFD0 to the GPS IFD pointer (tag 0x8825), then read GPSLatitudeRef/GPSLatitude (tags 1, 2) and GPSLongitudeRef/GPSLongitude (3, 4) as RATIONAL triples, and compute dec = d + m/60 + s/3600, negated for S/W. Only the first 128 KB is read via file.slice().arrayBuffer(). HEIC gets an honest message: 'export as JPEG — PictoTrack's desktop build handles this via Pillow'. 2) The map is a 1° land bitmask (360x180 bits, ~8 kB, about 2.7 kB gzipped). A one-off script in scripts/ generates it from Natural Earth 110m land, which is public domain. It renders as an SVG dot grid tinted with --accent, and the pin animates in with the MagicCircle sigil. 3) Optional reverse geocode through a new edge route that calls Nominatim with an identifying User-Agent and caches the result. It reuses the contact route's in-memory rateLimited() pattern. If it fails or is offline, the panel shows coordinates and an openstreetmap.org/?mlat=&mlon= link. 4) The 'Try a sample' file is a generated image tagged with Kochi's real coordinates (site.coords: 09°55′N 76°16′E) and labelled as a sample; ideally the owner swaps in one of his own photos. 5) No GPS found: the pipeline diagram shows that PictoTrack would now try the OCR route, and states it runs in the desktop app (Tesseract.js stays out). 6) The panel is next/dynamic-loaded only when the PictoTrack modal opens. project.links stays {}.
proposals.risk: iOS's photo picker can strip location unless the user keeps 'Location' in the share options, so the no-GPS state has to be a first-class, well-explained outcome, not an error. Nominatim's usage policy needs low volume, caching and attribution, which the opt-in button plus rate limit cover. Privacy copy must be exact: nothing is uploaded and only coordinates are sent, and only on click. The panel must not imply OCR runs in the browser.
proposals.mobile: Best on phones: the file input opens the camera roll, so visitors test it on their own photos. The map is a single SVG of about 2.7 kB gzipped and three.js is never touched. The panel stacks under the case-study text and is fully tappable.

proposals.title: Spellbook: a ⌘K palette with a bilingual index that drives the page
proposals.pitch: ⌘K, Ctrl+K or '/' opens a grimoire-styled palette over a slowly turning MagicCircle seal. You can type 'carbon', 'maho', 魔法 or 'python' and every entity in content.ts answers: sections, case studies, timeline floors, hackathons, hobbies, socials, and skills with links to where each one is evidenced. Arrowing onto a section row live-crossfades the whole page's palette behind the dialog to that section's anime colours and shows its art plate in a preview pane. Pressing Enter 'casts': the panel collapses into a sigil that flies to the target and the page eases there. Commands cover theme, 剣/杖, sound, copy email, replay the intro, start the tour, plus a few hidden incantations.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CZ's ⌘K chip is navigation for one app. The Spellbook is the site's search, its settings and its secrets in one place, and it is bilingual (English, kanji and romaji all match). The live palette preview is a trick only this site can do, because its themes are @property channels that interpolate.
proposals.approach: 1) The shell (always loaded, ~1 kB): a keydown listener for Mod+K and '/' outside inputs, mirroring KonamiEgg's INPUT/TEXTAREA guard, plus visible triggers. The dialog itself is next/dynamic-imported on first press and prefetched with requestIdleCallback after the hero settles. 2) The index (src/lib/spells.ts) is built from content.ts: nav (label, jp, plus a romaji map such as sakuhin, shoukai, mahou, kiseki, shumi, renraku), projects, timeline, hackathons, hobbies, socials and skillGroups. Skill rows get cross-references derived automatically: skill names are matched against project.stack and timeline.tags through a small alias table (Python → PictoTrack and the InternVision intern row; React & TypeScript → CarbonZero). The percentages show exactly as written in content.ts. 3) Matching is a hand-written subsequence scorer with word-start and kanji-exact bonuses, with no fuzzy library. 4) Live preview: while a section row is active, set document.documentElement.dataset.section to it so the globals.css @property transitions crossfade. On close, restore whatever SectionTheme had. 5) Navigation: add a 'lenis:to' CustomEvent ({detail: {target, offset}}) to SmoothScroll.tsx, falling back to scrollIntoView under reduced motion. Case-study rows open the modal through a small context or the URL (see case-deeplinks). 6) The cast animation is a framer-motion fixed clone from the selected row's rect to the destination SectionHeader emblem's rect, in the same visual language as the Preloader's departure. 7) Hidden incantations, matched only on exact phrase: 'link start' (tour), 'recast' (replay the Preloader through a 'grimoire:recast' event that resets done/leaving), 'overdrive' (reveals the @gearshift.overdrive Instagram with a speed-line wipe). 8) A11y: role=dialog aria-modal; the input is role=combobox with aria-controls, aria-activedescendant and aria-expanded; a listbox of options; a focus trap reusing ProjectModal's Tab logic; Esc closes; focus is restored. 9) Telemetry fix in passing: start the section cell at '00 TOP', not nav[0].
proposals.risk: The live palette preview must be restored on every exit path (Esc, backdrop click, selecting a non-section row) or the page is left in the wrong theme. Debounce it so fast arrowing doesn't strobe; under reduced motion the @property transition is already 0.01ms, so it snaps cleanly. Hidden incantations must never be the only route to a feature: 'link start' and 'recast' are also listed commands. Keep the ⌘ glyph only on Mac (read navigator.userAgentData.platform) and show Ctrl elsewhere.
proposals.mobile: No keyboard on phones, so a 'Search the grimoire…' field heads the mobile menu overlay in Nav.tsx and opens the palette as a full-height sheet. The input stays above the software keyboard via visualViewport, and rows are 48px tap targets. The art preview pane is hidden below md, but the palette preview crossfade still plays behind the sheet. The chunk loads on first tap only.
removes: The duplicate IST clock in Nav.tsx (the xl-only <span> showing {clock} IST). Its slot becomes the ⌘K chip, since Telemetry already shows a live clock at lg and up
Telemetry's initial 'SECTION 01 WORK' reading on the hero and the 404 page

proposals.title: The six seals: collect the section glyphs and recast the circle
proposals.pitch: Each section's kanji (作品 紹介 魔法 軌跡 趣味 連絡) is quietly a seal you can claim. Click or tap it and it lifts off the header and flies into a 'SEALS 3/6' cell on the telemetry strip. Claim all six and the intro's hexagram is recast over the page as an encore: the six glyphs ignite at its points, 剣 and 杖 collide, and the hero sigil keeps the six glyphs on its rim from then on. The Konami code and two other themed secrets join the same ledger.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CZ has no secrets at all. This turns the site's own intro vocabulary into a collectible that pays off by replaying the showpiece people already liked. It is the screenshot-and-tell-a-friend moment, and it rewards people for scrolling all six sections.
proposals.approach: 1) src/lib/grimoire.ts: a tiny external store (useSyncExternalStore) holding {seals: Set<SectionId>, secrets: Set<string>}, persisted to localStorage with try/catch like ThemeProvider. 2) GlyphSeal.tsx replaces the aria-hidden jp <span> in SectionHeader.tsx and Contact.tsx with a real <button aria-label='Claim the 魔法 seal (Stack)' aria-pressed>. It gets a faint shimmer about every 14 s, only while in view (IntersectionObserver) and only motion-safe. 3) The claim flight is a fixed-position clone animated with framer-motion from the source rect to the Telemetry cell's rect, or to a six-slot bottom toast on phones. If sound is on (mana-audio), an ascending note plays. 4) Completion dispatches 'grimoire:recast' with {encore: true}. Preloader.tsx gains an encore mode that skips the name block and the sessionStorage gate and ends on a '六 / 六' seal instead of the departure. ManaCore.tsx adds six CanvasTexture sprites of the glyphs on its outer ring once all are claimed, and MagicCircle.tsx takes an optional glyphs-claimed prop so phones see the reward too. 5) The secrets ledger absorbs KonamiEgg.tsx: the Konami code becomes 'System view' (same outline effect, now counted), plus 'Duality overload' (five 剣/杖 flips within 3 s, which replays the Preloader's collision beat in the hero) and 'overdrive' (shared with the Spellbook). The Spellbook's 'Secrets' row shows found entries and hint-only silhouettes for the rest.
proposals.risk: Taste: the shimmer must stay a whisper, not a nag. Turning decorative spans into buttons adds six tab stops, so each needs a clear aria-label and the set should read as optional. CJK in a CanvasTexture renders with whatever system serif is available, which is acceptable for a reward. The encore must keep all three Preloader exits (finish, Skip/Esc, watchdog).
proposals.mobile: Tap to claim. With no telemetry strip below lg, claims fly into a slim six-slot toast pinned to the bottom of the screen that auto-hides after 2 s. The encore plays the existing SVG/framer Preloader (no WebGL), and the reward shows on the phone-only SVG MagicCircle, so phones get the full payoff without three.js.
removes: src/components/layout/KonamiEgg.tsx as a standalone component and its generic 'Wireframe mode' toast. The effect survives inside the secrets ledger

proposals.title: Hold to cast: a chargeable hero sigil and press feedback that works on phones
proposals.pitch: Press and hold the hero sigil (or hold Space while it is focused) and it spins up, its motes pull inward and the mana field bends toward it. Let go and a shockwave ring blows outward through the flow field. Hold to full charge (about 1.2 s) and the cast flips the 剣/杖 duality with a burst. The same 'cast' gesture, scaled down, gives every primary button a runic ring ripple from the exact press point. That is the first tap feedback phones have ever had on this site.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CZ's dotted globe is a backdrop. Here the centrepiece is a toy, and the duality switch, the site's thesis, becomes something you perform rather than a 36px pill. The ripple covers the gap the touch hooks leave: phones currently get no hover, tilt or magnetic feedback at all.
proposals.approach: 1) Hero.tsx: keep the decorative wrapper aria-hidden and add a sibling focusable <button aria-label='Charge the sigil — hold to switch Sword/Wand'> over the sigil's area. It handles pointerdown/up/cancel and keydown/up for Space and Enter, and drives a 0..1 charge with an rAF ramp. 2) ManaCore.tsx reads charge from a 'mana:charge' CustomEvent stored in a ref. The tick loop multiplies ring speeds by (1 + 4c), lerps mote radius toward 0.6r, and raises disc opacity. On release it spawns an expanding LineLoop ring (scale 1 to 2.2, opacity to 0, 600 ms). 3) FlowField.tsx gets a 'flow:impulse' listener ({x, y, strength}) that adds a decaying radial push, reusing the existing repulsion maths. 4) At full charge it calls useTheme().toggleAccent(). 5) useCast.ts plus CastRipple.tsx: on pointerdown, append an absolutely positioned SVG ring (dashed stroke in --accent, CSS transform scale 0 to 1 plus fade, 450 ms) at the press point inside overflow-hidden buttons. Apply it to Nav 'Let's talk', the hero Scroll disc, Contact's email pill and Send button, project cards, skill tabs and footer back-to-top. Optionally call navigator.vibrate(8) on Android. 6) Touch parity for hover-only reveals: a centre-line IntersectionObserver (the SectionTheme rule) sets data-inview on Process cards and project cards, and Tailwind group-data-[inview] variants mirror the group-hover reveals (Process kanji 観描造磨, the card sigil, the accent sweep). 7) Reduced motion: no spin or shockwave; a full hold or press still flips the accent instantly, and the ripple becomes a 120 ms opacity flash.
proposals.risk: The charge button overlaps body text at some widths (the sigil frames the headline), so limit its hit area to the sigil's inner radius and keep it under the CTA's stacking order. Long-press on iOS can trigger text selection or callouts; use -webkit-touch-callout:none and user-select:none on the button only. The shockwave must stay subtle in light theme, where additive blending is already off.
proposals.mobile: The SVG MagicCircle that bleeds off the top-right on phones becomes the charge target: CSS variable-driven spin-up of its animate-spin-slow groups plus a ring pulse. No three.js loads. The tap ripple is most valuable here, as the only press feedback phones get. Hover-only content now reveals as cards cross the screen centre.
removes: The Magnetic wrappers around the six desktop nav links in Nav.tsx. They move 13px targets under the pointer; Magnetic stays on the round CTAs (Let's talk, Scroll, back-to-top) where it reads as play rather than drift

proposals.title: 'Link Start': a guided tour that locks onto real evidence
proposals.pitch: A 'Tour 案内' chip in the hero status row, and the 'link start' incantation, begin a six-stop walk-through in SAO-style system frames. At each stop the page eases to the element, HUD corner brackets snap and lock onto it, and the rest of the page dims through a cut-out mask. Stops: the sourced stat strip, the CarbonZero card, PictoTrack's 'Cast it yourself', the Intern floor of the timeline, the hackathon list and the email CTA. A short card says why it matters, in his voice and taken from content.ts. It ends with '6 / 6 floors cleared' and focus parked on the contact form.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CZ has a 'Tour' button and a 'Guided Tour' pill (main-0.png). Theirs is product onboarding. Ours is a recruiter's three-minute pitch, each claim pinned to the element that backs it. It is keyboard-first, narrated through aria-live, and themed so that every lock-on recolours with the section it lands in.
proposals.approach: 1) src/lib/tour.ts: an array of {selector, sectionId, title, body, jp} whose copy is drawn only from content.ts fields (intro.stats notes, projects[].summary, timeline[1].description, hackathons.length), so nothing is invented. Elements get data-tour='…' hooks. 2) Tour.tsx (next/dynamic, loaded on start): a fixed full-screen SVG with a <mask> rect cut-out (rx 6) whose bounds follow the target's getBoundingClientRect in an rAF loop while scrolling. Four HUD corner brackets (the .hud-frame look) spring from viewport corners to the target. A card is positioned by a small hand-rolled placement routine (above/below, flipped by space), with no floating-ui. 3) Navigation through the 'lenis:to' event (added in spellbook-cmdk). Lenis stays running so the mask tracks the target, while wheel and touch input are blocked by an overlay. 4) Controls: Next/Back buttons, arrow keys, Esc to exit, and progress pips showing the six section kanji. The step text is mirrored into an aria-live='polite' region, and focus moves to the card's heading each step. 5) Mana-audio, if enabled, plays SAO-style two-note 'system' blips on lock-on. 6) The 404 page (not-found.tsx) gets 'Lost? Link start' to launch it on the home page through a ?tour=1 parameter.
proposals.risk: The mask has to track targets that animate in (Reveal, TextReveal), so wait for the Lenis scroll to settle and re-measure on ResizeObserver. If a stop's element is missing, the tour must skip it rather than hang. Do not let it auto-launch: a tour that ambushes first-time visitors is worse than none.
proposals.mobile: The card becomes a bottom sheet (safe-area aware) with large Next/Back buttons and swipe left/right; the spotlight still tracks above it. Six stops fit in about 60 s of tapping, and the code loads only when the chip is tapped.

proposals.title: Mana audio: opt-in synthesized sound, one timbre per anime section
proposals.pitch: A small 音 toggle in the nav (and a Spellbook command) turns on a quiet layer of sound, generated live and never from samples. Crossing into Work lands a low grimoire thud, About crackles with electric noise, Stack chimes like an FM bell, Path blips like an SAO system window, and Contact plucks a soft kalimba note. The palette crossfade you already see becomes something you hear. Nav hovers climb a pentatonic scale by section index, 剣/杖 plays a fifth up or down, opening a case study is a page-turn swish, and replaying the intro scores every beat of the cast.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CZ is silent. This makes the section themes multi-sensory with zero asset weight and nothing copyrighted. Every sound is an oscillator or filtered noise written in code, and it is off until the visitor asks for it.
proposals.approach: 1) src/lib/sfx.ts is lazy-imported on first enable. It builds one AudioContext created inside the toggle's click (which satisfies iOS's gesture unlock), a master GainNode at about -20 dB, a DynamicsCompressor, and a ConvolverNode with a 1.2 s decaying-noise impulse generated in code. 2) Voices, all at 1–3 voices and under 400 ms: work is a sawtooth at 73 Hz through a lowpass sweeping 900 to 200 Hz plus a short bandpassed noise 'page'; about is three to five random 4 ms noise impulses through a 2.5 kHz bandpass (crackle); stack is FM (carrier sine, modulator ratio 3.5, index decaying 6 to 0); path is a square two-note blip (E6 then B6, 60 ms each); contact is a triangle pluck with a long reverb send; hobby and the default are a sine pluck. 3) Hooks: SectionTheme.tsx dispatches 'grimoire:section' whenever it writes data-section, nav links fire on pointerenter and focus, and ThemeProvider toggles fire their interval. Preloader 'recast' schedules notes at its B beat offsets: rings, then six glyph notes at 0.13 s steps, then the collision. The Spellbook, glyph seals and contact 'sent' each get a cue. 4) The preference is stored in localStorage 'sound'. Nothing plays on first load before a gesture, the context is suspended on visibilitychange, and new sounds are dropped if more than 4 are active. 5) The toggle's waveform bars animate only when sound is on and motion is allowed.
proposals.risk: Taste is the whole risk: it must be quiet and sparse, with no sound on scroll ticks or every hover. Clipping or harsh square waves on laptop speakers, so cap levels and lowpass the path blips. Safari can resume the AudioContext late, so the first sound after enable may need the toggle's own click as warm-up. The pressed state must be exposed (aria-pressed) and labelled 'Sound effects', not just an icon.
proposals.mobile: Works on phones: the toggle sits in the mobile menu and the Spellbook sheet. Tap sounds fire on pointerdown for instant feedback, and the module is under 3 kB gzipped and loads only when enabled. iOS's silent switch mutes WebAudio, which is the correct behaviour.

proposals.title: Shareable spells: portal the case study, give each project a URL, share card and copy moments
proposals.pitch: Opening a case study now updates the address to /work/carbonzero, so a recruiter can paste one project to a colleague. That link unfurls as its own card: project palette, title, stack, and the same generative geometry as the tile. The modal finally sits above everything, so its close button works, and it gains 'Share' (the native sheet on phones) and 'Copy link' with a small 共有 toast. The email gets a one-tap copy beside the mailto. A successful contact message shows a 'summons seal' receipt: a MagicCircle seeded from the sender's name and the send time.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CZ is a single page with one share preview. Here every project is a linkable, crawlable page with its own preview card. The receipt seal turns the dullest moment on any portfolio, 'Message sent', into the one thing a visitor screenshots.
proposals.approach: 1) Bug fix first: render ProjectModal through createPortal(…, document.body). It is currently trapped inside #work's 'isolate' stacking context (Projects.tsx), so a hit test at the close button's centre lands on the Nav on both 390px and 1440px, and the Petals canvas at z-[1] draws over the panel. Give the portal z-[10002] so it sits above Telemetry and Nav, and stop the nav pill overlapping its top edge. 2) Extract a <CaseStudy project> body from ProjectModal. Add src/app/work/[id]/page.tsx using generateStaticParams over projects and generateMetadata, so a hard load renders a full page. On the home page, opening a card calls history.pushState({}, '', '/work/'+id) and popstate closes it, so the back button behaves. 3) src/app/work/[id]/opengraph-image.tsx is an ImageResponse (edge) in the style of the existing opengraph-image.tsx. It uses project.palette, title, subtitle and the first four stack items, and draws ring geometry like ProjectArtwork variant 0. It deliberately does not use the JAPAN RAMEN face, because an OG card is promotional use under its licence. 4) Share: navigator.share({title, text: project.summary, url}) when available, otherwise navigator.clipboard.writeText with a role=status toast. 5) Contact.tsx 'sent' state: MagicCircle seeded by a string hash of name plus ISO minute, with 'Summons received · <IST time>', using real values only. 6) sitemap.ts adds /work/[id]. PictoTrack's links stay {}; the page simply shows no repo button, as now.
proposals.risk: pushState must not trigger App Router navigation (use window.history directly, not router.push), and Lenis must be stopped and started symmetrically on popstate. A stand-alone /work/[id] page needs the layout chrome (Telemetry, Nav) without the Preloader replaying. sessionStorage gating already covers that, but a direct cold visit should probably skip the intro. The OG route runs on edge, so keep it free of Node APIs.
proposals.mobile: Phones get the native share sheet: the most natural share moment there is, and the one a recruiter scrolling LinkedIn on a phone will use. The close button becomes tappable again (the confirmed bug is worst at 390px, where the nav pill covers it). The copy-email button is a 44px target beside the CTA, which matters on phones without a configured mail app.
removes: The modal-inside-#work rendering that hides the close button under the nav and lets petals draw over the case study

proposals.title: Episode title cards: section openers that write their own kanji
proposals.pitch: Each section opens like an anime episode title card. A Mincho slate (第壱話 to 第陸話) sits beside a mono 'EPISODE 01 — GRIMOIRE'. The heading pairs a condensed grotesque line in ink with an italic-serif line in the section accent. Down the right edge, the section's kanji (作品, 紹介, 魔法, 軌跡, 趣味, 連絡) stand 300px tall in tategaki and write themselves in correct stroke order as you arrive. Thin accent-2 construction strokes trace each stroke, which brings in the SAO HUD, and the heavy Mincho ink floods in underneath. These are the same six glyphs the preloader lights on the hexagram, so the intro finally pays off: it casts them, and each chapter writes its own.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero's '(01) —— MANIFESTO' label and sans + italic-serif heading are a borrowed Swiss editorial convention, and they are static. This keeps the scale and the serif turn, then adds a vocabulary that is native to Mishal: episode slates and calligraphy drawn from real stroke-order data. A climate dashboard can't claim that, and no template has it. The heading goes from 76px to about 144px at 1440, which matches CarbonZero's scale. See pd-mid.png, pd-done.png and pm-mid.png.
proposals.approach: 1) scripts/build-kanji.mjs, run manually and committed. For every character in nav[].jp plus the slate numerals 第壱弐参肆伍陸話, it fetches KanjiVG kanji/{codepoint}.svg, extracts the ordered stroke paths (`kvg:XXXX-sN`), and writes src/lib/kanji/strokes.json (about 7 KB gzipped) with a CC BY-SA 3.0 header. 2) The same script reads glyph ink bounds from the subset font (opentype.js) and stores a per-glyph fit matrix, so stroke centrelines land on the Mincho glyph. The prototype computes this at runtime with getBBox; see kanji-fit.png. 3) New src/components/ui/KanjiWrite.tsx: one <svg viewBox='0 0 109 109'> per character with a faint ghost <text> glyph, the ink <text> masked by a <mask> of KanjiVG strokes (stroke-width 15, pathLength=1, dashoffset animated per stroke), and a hairline copy of the strokes at stroke-width .8 in rgb(var(--accent-2)). The animation is a framer-motion timeline that starts once useInView fires: each stroke's duration is proportional to its path length (about 70ms per 10 units) with a 120ms pause between characters, so 作品 takes about 1.5s. On completion the mask is removed so no stroke gaps remain, and the hairlines fade to .25. 4) Rewrite SectionHeader.tsx as a 12-column grid: slate at cols 1–6, plate at 6–10, kanji column at 11–12 spanning the rows, heading at the bottom of cols 1–8, and a footer rule with '( N° 00X ) · series' plus the standfirst. Line 1 uses text-fg; line 2 uses font-serif italic text-accent. Drop the emblem. 5) Contact.tsx's hand-rolled header switches to the same component with size='display'. 6) Add a `kanjiNumeral(index)` util in src/lib/utils.ts. 7) Add KanjiVG (CC BY-SA 3.0) and Shippori Mincho (OFL) to credits.assets.
proposals.risk: KanjiVG is CC BY-SA 3.0. The derived strokes.json has to stay share-alike and be credited, so keep it a separate data file with its own licence. A few glyphs (法, 剣) leave small mask gaps until completion; removing the mask at the end fixes that. Stroke data or a font miss for a character should fall back to the plain glyph. Reduced motion renders the finished glyph with static hairlines. The kanji column is aria-hidden and the English h2 keeps the semantics. Taste risk: done at half conviction, a 300px kanji column becomes wallpaper, so it needs full scale and one column only.
proposals.mobile: The column shrinks to about 30vw in the right gutter and sits behind the heading (z-index 0). The heading drops to 17.5vw condensed, which fits 'Things I have' on one line at 390px. The plate becomes a full-width panel underneath (pm-mid.png). Cost: about 7 KB of JSON code-split into the header chunk and a 10–15 KB font subset. No three.js; the strokes are SVG.
removes: SectionEmblem in headers
'( N° 00X ) — LABEL' as the lead element (demoted to the footer rule)
16px decorative kanji beside the label
the all-accent two-line heading

proposals.title: One print process for five plates
proposals.pitch: Stop pretending the character art is cut out. Every plate becomes a hard-edged manga panel with a clipped corner and a 2px accent keyline. It rests as a two-tone halftone screen print in that section's palette, then one per-anime 'cut' wipes the real colour in: a diagonal anti-magic slash for Black Clover, a lightning-bolt split for MHA, an iris opening from the wand tip for Wistoria, scan-line rows for SAO, and a soft petal bloom for Kaoru Hana. Light-ground plates settle as colour printed onto a deep section tint, so the white rectangles disappear. A credit line under each panel names the series, its Japanese title, and the creator and studio.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero's imagery is a single consistent stock photo treatment. Ours are five sources in five unrelated styles (plates.png), and today the feathered rectangles look pasted on. A single print process turns them into a set that recolours with the @property crossfade, and the reveal cuts give each anime its own motion signature. Compare plate-test.png and plate-test-contact.png ('today' against options A and C), and pd-duo-2.png against pd-done-2.png.
proposals.approach: Rewrite SectionVisual.tsx as <Plate>. A wrapper with `clip-path: polygon(0 0,100% 0,100% 86%,90% 100%,0 100%)` holds three layers. (a) Duotone: a container with background rgb(var(--accent)); the img gets `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.15)` and `mix-blend-mode: multiply`; an ::after layer with background color-mix(in srgb, rgb(var(--accent)) 18%, rgb(var(--bg))) and `mix-blend-mode: lighten`. This is pure CSS, so it follows the --c1/--c2 @property channels. (b) Halftone: a ::before with radial-gradient dots at 4px, multiply, opacity .55. (c) The colour layer, revealed by an animated clip-path per `cut`. Dark-ground plates (work, about) end in raw colour. Light-ground plates (stack, path, contact) end as colour with multiply over color-mix(accent 70%, bg) plus the dots, which is option C in plate-test.png. Per-plate config goes in content.ts as sectionThemes.*.plate = { src, ground, focus: '50% 22%', ratio: '3/2' | '4/5', cut }, so crops are art-directed with object-position instead of guessed. Height is capped at 52vh so portrait plates such as stack.webp can't push the heading off-screen. The caption reads from credits.series. Light theme: the shadow maps to rgb(var(--fg)) and the highlight to a paper tint, both automatic through the same variables. The reveal triggers once at 40% of the viewport via useInView.
proposals.risk: Some will see duotone as dulling the owner's art. That is why it resolves to colour, and only light grounds keep the tint. mix-blend-mode needs `isolation: isolate` on the panel or it bleeds into the section wash. Clip-path cuts are cheap, but keep the reveal one-shot. Reduced motion shows the final state with no wipe. The plates stay decorative (alt=''), and the credit is visible text, which strengthens the attribution the footer already gives.
proposals.mobile: Plates become full-bleed-width panels under the heading instead of 210px right-aligned feathered floats. Each keeps its own ratio and focal crop, and the credit line wraps under it (pm-mid.png). No extra JS beyond the existing useInView.
removes: FADE four-sided feather mask
opacity .82 'ghosted' plates
SectionVisualMobile right-aligned 210px float
SectionArt SVG fallbacks as the visible default (keep only as a missing-src fallback)

proposals.title: Type system: a condensed display cut, ink/accent heading split, one real Japanese face, Inter dropped
proposals.pitch: Big headlines change register. 'Things I have' in Bricolage condensed at the font's display optical size reads like a manga cover line, and the italic serif answers it in the section colour. Body text moves to Bricolage at text optical size, so the site speaks in one grotesque voice instead of Bricolage plus Inter. Every Japanese character, from the 300px kanji to the 11px katakana in Hobby and Footer, renders in Shippori Mincho B1 on every OS instead of whatever serif the device happens to have.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero's display face is one tight grotesque at one width. We get two expressive widths from one family, plus a real Mincho, a real italic serif and the Japan Ramen wordmark. Each face has a single job, which means more range at fewer bytes. The bilingual typography is consistent and intentional, where CarbonZero is English-only.
proposals.approach: 1) Build a display cut with fontTools varLib.instancer: Bricolage at opsz 96, wdth 75, wght 600–800, about 36 KB (measured in artdirection/dl/brico-cond.woff2). Load it via next/font/local as --font-display-cond. Keep the existing next/font/google Bricolage (41 KB, opsz 14) as body and UI text and point --font-sans at it. Remove Inter from layout.tsx: 48 KB of preloaded font gone, and total font weight drops from about 89 KB to about 77 KB. 2) tailwind.config.ts gets fontFamily.cond and fontFamily.jp. 3) globals.css: `.display-cond { font-family: var(--font-display-cond); font-stretch: 75%; letter-spacing: -0.025em; line-height: .84 }`, a new `.h-mega` at clamp(3.4rem, 10.2vw, 10rem) for openers, `.h-section` kept for sub-heads, and `.jp` repointed to var(--font-jp). 4) TextReveal.tsx line 0 uses text-fg and line 1 uses font-serif italic text-accent; the heading is no longer entirely accent. 5) scripts/subset-jp.mjs collects every CJK character from src/**/*.ts(x) (71 today, plus slate numerals), runs pyftsubset or subset-font on Shippori Mincho B1 800, and writes a woff2 of about 25 KB. Load it via next/font/local with preload:false and display:swap. Hangul (한국어) stays on the system fallback. 6) Optional kinetic touch on motion-safe openers only: animate the condensed headline's letter-spacing from .04em to -.025em as it reveals, so it settles like a drawn bow. This avoids animating width, which forces reflow.
proposals.risk: Dropping Inter changes body texture. Bricolage at opsz 14 is quirkier, so check long paragraphs in About, where line-height may need to go to 1.6. The subset font has to be regenerated whenever content.ts gains a new CJK character; add a check in the script that fails CI if any character is missing. All new fonts are SIL OFL, so nothing new attaches to the personal-use Japan Ramen licence, and Japan Ramen stays on the name only.
proposals.mobile: Condensed display fits about 40% more characters per line, so phone headings can grow from 2.6rem to 17.5vw (about 68px) without breaking mid-phrase. Total font payload goes down. No JS change.
removes: Inter (next/font/google) — 48 KB preloaded
OS-dependent CJK fallback via Instrument Serif stack
all-accent headings

proposals.title: Work as grimoire spreads, with the real artifacts
proposals.pitch: The bento of placeholder rings and bars is replaced by two full-width spreads, one 'page' per project. Each has a Mincho numeral (壱, 弐), the title in condensed display at about 9vw, an italic-serif subtitle, and a mono metadata row (year, role, context, status). The facing page holds the real artifact. For CarbonZero that is two committed screenshots of the live site, the hero and the 'since 1750' intro, overlapped like proof sheets. For PictoTrack, which has no live surface, it is a typeset diagram of its actual two-route pipeline, taken straight from its description. The case-study modal stays one click away.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: The reference is his own project, so the portfolio puts it on the page: CarbonZero's interface becomes a captioned figure in Mishal's spread. CarbonZero's 'Measure / Explore / Plan & save' rows are large type with no artifact. These are large type with proof. See spread-d.png and spread-m.png.
proposals.approach: 1) scripts/capture-work.mjs (Playwright, run by the owner locally; it's his own site) captures carbon-footprint-calc-v5.vercel.app at 1440×900 (hero and intro) to public/work/carbonzero-home.webp and carbonzero-intro.webp, and records the capture date. The caption shows the real URL and that date. It is not claimed as live. 2) content.ts: projects[].shots?: {src, w, h, caption}[], and projects[].pipeline?: {label, steps[]}[] for PictoTrack, built only from the existing description (Greyscale → Otsu → Dilation → Tesseract → Nominatim; fallback EXIF GPS → DMS→decimal → ±hemisphere; reverse geocode → gmplot). links stays {} exactly as it is. 3) Projects.tsx: replace the TILES grid, Tilt cards and hover MagicCircle with a <Spread> component on a 12-column grid. Numeral at col 1, title block at 2–7, page at 8–12; alternate sides for every second spread. Screenshots get the clipped-corner panel from screen-print-plates. The second shot is offset -56px to break the bottom edge, which adds grid tension. 4) New src/components/ui/Pipeline.tsx renders the steps as bordered mono nodes with accent arrows, as semantic <ol>s. 5) The title stays a button that opens the existing ProjectModal. The filter UI stays hidden while there is only one category.
proposals.risk: Screenshots go stale whenever CarbonZero ships; the caption carries the capture date so that is honest. Without the owner running the capture script, the CarbonZero page falls back to the typographic block alone, so nothing is ever fabricated. Two spreads take more vertical space than the bento; cap each at about 90vh on desktop. Use next/image with explicit width and height to avoid CLS.
proposals.mobile: Single column: numeral and title, metadata wrapped into two rows, then one screenshot at full width. The second overlapping shot is hidden; the pipeline nodes wrap (spread-m.png). Images are lazy next/image webp at about 60–90 KB each.

TILES bento spans
Tilt on project cards

proposals.title: About: the person as a photograph, the manifesto at CarbonZero scale
proposals.pitch: He is a photographer, so his portrait should be framed like one, not shown in a rounded avatar card. The portrait gets large and bleeds off the left edge of the container. A film-rebate edge with sprocket holes and decorative frame numbers runs along it, and the duotone MHA plate tucks over its top-right corner as a small inset panel, the way manga uses an inset panel: the person and the influence in one composition. The caption sits on the photo's baseline (the owner's TODO caption, unchanged). Below it, the three scroll-highlight paragraphs grow to CarbonZero's manifesto scale, and a few phrases turn into italic serif as they light up.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero's only human imagery is stock forest and ocean. Ours is the actual person, framed with the craft he claims (photography), next to the art he loves. Its manifesto (cz/main-800.png) is the benchmark for scale; we match it and tie the italic turns to his own words ('a camera', 'deciding what to leave out').
proposals.approach: About.tsx: remove the separate header plate and pass the portrait into the opener's plate slot for this section only, with the Deku plate as `inset`. proposals.title: PictoTrack's pipeline, runnable on your own photo, with nothing uploaded
proposals.pitch: PictoTrack has no repo or live link, and that empty link stays as the owner left it, so the chapter proves the work by letting you run it. Drop in a photo, or use the labelled demo file, and watch the fallback route run in your browser: EXIF block found → GPSLatitude rationals → degrees-minutes-seconds to decimal → hemisphere sign flip → coordinates. Next to it, the OCR route's preprocessing really runs (greyscale, Otsu threshold with the value it chose, dilation) and shows each bitmap. Tesseract appears as a labelled stage that runs in the desktop app only.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero visualises the world's data. This makes the visitor's own file the data, processed on their device, with every intermediate value shown. The pipeline that content.ts describes in prose (OpenCV greyscale → Otsu → dilation; EXIF degrees-minutes-seconds → decimal with hemisphere handling) becomes something you can run, without a repo or a hosting bill.
proposals.approach:
src/lib/exif-gps.ts, about 90 lines with no dependency: scan the JPEG for the APP1 'Exif\0\0' segment, read the TIFF byte order (II/MM), go from IFD0 via tag 0x8825 to the GPS IFD, and read tags 1–4 (LatRef, Lat as 3 RATIONALs, LonRef, Lon). decimal = d + m/60 + s/3600, negated for S or W, mirroring PictoTrack's logic.

src/workers/preprocess.worker.ts: downscale to ≤1024px, then Rec.601 greyscale, a 256-bin histogram, Otsu (maximise between-class variance, about 25 lines) and a 3×3 dilation. It returns three ImageBitmaps plus the threshold.

PipelineBench.tsx: an SVG with two lanes (OCR, EXIF) merging into 'reverse-geocode → map'. Stages light up as they complete, and an aria-live region announces results. Input is a visible <label> with an <input type=file accept='image/*'> plus drag-and-drop.

Output is the coordinates plus an 'Open in OpenStreetMap ↗' link the visitor chooses to click. There is no automatic geocoding call, so their location never leaves the device.

The demo JPEG is generated in the browser with a hand-built GPS IFD at site.coords (Kochi) and labelled 'demo file — GPS written by this page'. HEIC files and files without GPS get honest messages.

Loaded with next/dynamic (ssr:false) only when the chapter is near the viewport. Estimated under 8 kB gzipped; no WASM, no three.js. Labelled 'a browser re-implementation of PictoTrack's fallback route'.
proposals.risk: Privacy perception: it must say 'processed on your device, never uploaded' and actually make zero network calls, checked in devtools. Many shared photos have GPS stripped, so 'no GPS in this file' has to read as a normal outcome. It must not pretend to be PictoTrack, hence the re-implementation label. The diagram needs a text-list equivalent.
proposals.mobile: Works well on phones: the file input opens the camera roll. iOS may strip location unless 'Include location' is chosen in the picker, and that is handled with a message. Lanes stack vertically. The Web Worker and the downscale keep it responsive, with no heavy libraries.

src/lib/github.ts (server-only), getGithub() fetches:
- users/MishalxRSET
- repos?sort=pushed

- /languages

proposals.title: First paint is the cast: an SSR-gated intro and a hero that doesn't wait for hydration
proposals.pitch: First-time visitors see the black summoning field on the very first painted frame. Today the nav and an empty hero sit on screen for about 1.5 s before the cast mounts; that flash goes away. Returning visitors get the name itself as the first contentful paint: a brush-stroke ink reveal sweeps across MOHAMMED MISHAL starting at first paint, not after 191 KB of JS hydrates. proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero's intro is a separate data-driven loader. Here the cast is in the first frame with no flash of the site chrome, and the theatre costs nothing in Core Web Vitals: the largest paint is the wordmark at FCP, so a 4.75 s intro and a green LCP can coexist.
proposals.approach: (1) layout.tsx themeScript also sets el.dataset.intro='play' when sessionStorage 'preloaded' is unset and matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') is false. Preloader.tsx always server-renders its opening frame (the #07080c field, the grid lines and the outer ring) inside <div data-preloader>. globals.css adds `html:not([data-intro=play]) [data-preloader]{display:none}`. The component reads the attribute instead of the current useState(true)/useEffect pattern, so hydration adopts the same DOM and nothing flashes. While the intro plays, the overlay gets role=dialog, aria-modal and aria-label='Intro', the Skip button gets focus, and #main, header and footer are set to `inert`; all of that is removed on release. (2) Hero.tsx moves the above-the-fold entrance from framer `initial` (SSR'd as inline opacity:0) to CSS keyframes in globals.css with animation delays of 300 ms or less, so the animation starts at first paint. The h1 becomes one text block revealed by an animated mask: `mask-image: linear-gradient(100deg,#000 40%,transparent 60%)`, `mask-size: 250% 100%`, and a 900 ms `ink` keyframe on mask-position. Opacity never hits 0, so the h1 (about 260k px² on desktop) is the LCP candidate at FCP and outranks the preloader wordmark (34k px²). CharReveal stays for small strings only. (3) The name font switches to localFont `display:'block'`. It is 6.9 KB and already preloaded, and this avoids FOUT-driven CLS once the h1 paints early. (4) Add `<noscript><style>[style*="opacity:0"],[style*="translateY(110%)"]{opacity:1!important;transform:none!important}</style></noscript>` to the layout head. Counter.tsx SSRs the real value, with aria-hidden animated digits plus an sr-only final value. (5) Verify with the existing LCP observer harness (perf.mjs). Targets: mobile LCP 2.0 s or less at 4x CPU and 1.6 Mbps (today 5404 ms), desktop 0.8 s or less, CLS 0.02 or less.
proposals.risk: The 'h1 under the overlay still wins LCP' step assumes Chrome's LCP does not discount occluded elements. I have not verified that, so check it with the harness; if it fails, scale the preloader wordmark below the hero's painted area. proposals.title: One heartbeat: one store for section, palette and motion (the browser changes anime, plus a 静 stillness switch)
proposals.pitch: Scrolling from Black Clover through MHA, Wistoria and SAO to Fragrant Flower, the phone's own address-bar area crossfades crimson, green, purple, cyan, pink along with the page. The nav pill slides to the section you are reading. The petals fall in the colours of the section you're actually in; today they lag one anime behind. A small 静 (stillness) switch in the telemetry strip and the mobile menu freezes every ambient loop (petals, flow field, sigil, marquees, scan line) for anyone who wants a still page, and weak phones drop to a lighter tier automatically.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero's pill nav marks the active page and its ticker is live. This marks the active section, carries the theme beyond the viewport into the browser UI itself, and gives visitors explicit control over motion, which nothing in the reference captures offers.
proposals.approach: New src/lib/runtime.ts: a tiny external store (subscribe/getSnapshot) holding {section, theme, accent, tier, palette}, read through useSyncExternalStore in src/hooks/useRuntime.ts. SectionTheme.tsx becomes the only IntersectionObserver writer; Telemetry's duplicate observer is removed. The hero becomes section 'prologue', and Telemetry shows '00 序 Prologue' instead of today's wrong '01 Work'. Palette pairs move to src/lib/palettes.ts as data, using the same numbers as globals.css (the audit checks parity), so canvases never call getComputedStyle. That fixes the measured stale-palette bug; FlowField and Petals instead lerp toward store targets over 700 ms in their own loop. New ThemeColor.tsx writes <meta name=theme-color> with the section's background wash (color-mix of accent 9% into bg, computed in TS), on section or theme change only. Remove the prefers-color-scheme themeColor pair from layout.tsx. In Nav.tsx, the active pill uses framer layoutId plus aria-current="location". Motion governor in src/lib/ticker.ts: one rAF, driven from SmoothScroll's Lenis loop, passes dt in ms to registered effects. ManaCore, FlowField and Petals become time-based, so 120/144 Hz screens stop running them 2 to 2.4 times too fast. Tiers: full; lite, chosen once after the intro when the median dt over 90 frames exceeds 22 ms or hardwareConcurrency is 4 or less (FlowField particles divided by 3, DPR 1, palette snaps with a 250 ms background fade instead of six @property channels restyling about 790 elements per frame); and still, from the 静 toggle (aria-pressed, persisted in localStorage) or prefers-reduced-motion. Still means html[data-motion=still] pauses CSS animations (marquee, spin-slow, scan-line, pulse-ring), Lenis is destroyed, framer gets MotionConfig reducedMotion="always", and canvases render one static frame that re-renders on palette or theme change (ManaCore currently goes stale). Petals.tsx becomes CSS petals: 6 to 10 inline SVG petals with transform keyframes (compositor only, no per-frame JS), filled with rgb(var(--accent)) so they crossfade with the page for free. A single useClock() store with one 1 Hz interval replaces the 3 intervals. Telemetry only mounts at lg and up.
proposals.risk: theme-color tinting is honoured by iOS Safari and Chrome Android but ignored by most desktop browsers, so it's a bonus layer. Update the meta only on section change, never per scroll frame. Auto-tiering must not demote a fast device: decide once, after the intro, and let the switch override. Palette numbers would live in both TS and CSS, so parity has to be tested.
proposals.mobile: The address-bar tint is phone-only and is the payoff here. CSS petals, one clock and an unmounted Telemetry remove the perpetual full-screen canvas and the scroll-rate setState that phones pay for today.

proposals.title: Every page of the grimoire gets a URL, a share card and a native morph
proposals.pitch: Clicking a project card morphs its artwork straight into the case study with a shared-element view transition, and the address bar becomes /work/carbonzero. That URL is shareable, the back button closes it, and opening it directly gives a full page. Shared links unfurl as generated cards in that section's palette, with original sigil geometry, the name, and the italic-serif second line. The sun/moon toggle sweeps the new theme in as a circle expanding from the button. The 剣/杖 switch either cuts the page with a diagonal sword slash or blooms it from a wand point.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero links out to separate tools (Calculator, Planner, Design Doc). Here each project is a deep-linkable page whose preview card is generated from the site's own sigil system, and the morphs are native browser transitions costing about 1 KB of JS.
proposals.approach: Routes: src/app/work/[slug]/page.tsx is a server component with generateStaticParams and generateMetadata driven by projects in content.ts. It renders the case-study body, extracted from Projects.tsx into src/components/sections/CaseStudy.tsx. Opening in-page keeps the modal, syncs the URL with window.history.pushState(null,'','/work/'+id) (Next 15 integrates native pushState with usePathname), and closes on popstate. Direct loads get the static page. OG: redesign src/app/opengraph-image.tsx and add src/app/work/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx and twitter-image.tsx, all on next/og ImageResponse. Fonts are OFL TTFs committed under src/app/og/fonts (Bricolage Grotesque, Instrument Serif italic). Never use JAPAN RAMEN: its licence forbids promotional use, and a share card is promotional. The sigil is MagicCircle/ProjectArtwork geometry serialised to an SVG data-URI , and colours come from palettes.ts. Also add apple-icon.tsx and manifest.ts, and list /work/* in sitemap.ts. View transitions: src/lib/transition.ts exports withTransition(update, kind, origin), which calls document.startViewTransition(() => flushSync(update)) and falls back to a plain update when the API is missing or the tier is reduced/still. On t.ready it runs document.documentElement.animate({clipPath:[...]}, {pseudoElement:'::view-transition-new(root)', duration:520, easing:'cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)'}): a circle from the button for theme, a polygon diagonal sweep for 剣, a circle with a ring for 杖. Card morph: set style.viewTransitionName='art-'+id on the clicked card's artwork and on the modal hero art only for the duration, and skip framer's modal entrance when the API exists. globals.css: `::view-transition-old(root),::view-transition-new(root){animation:none;mix-blend-mode:normal}`.
proposals.risk: Browsers without view-transition support get an instant swap. A duplicate view-transition-name aborts the transition, so set the name on the two involved elements only. A running transition swallows input, so keep each one at 520 ms or less. PictoTrack's empty links object is an owner placeholder: its page must render with no Live or Source buttons and must not invent any. The committed OG TTFs add about 300 KB to the repo and nothing to the client.
proposals.mobile: The card-to-page morph works on iOS 18+ and Chrome Android. The theme sweep is a cheap compositor clip-path. Links shared in WhatsApp or Instagram DMs, where this audience actually shares, unfurl into proper cards.

proposals.title: Keyboard parity, with focus drawn as a HUD target-lock
proposals.pitch: Tab through the site and focus appears as SAO-style corner brackets that snap onto each control: a target-lock reticle that is also a compliant focus indicator. It is keyboard-only and never follows the mouse. The skip link actually skips, nav links hand focus to the section you jump to, the skill tabs work like real tabs with arrow keys, and the mobile menu and the intro are proper modal layers. Screen readers hear the full name, the real stat values, and which section is current.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: The polish visible in the CarbonZero captures is visual. This makes the same level of polish operable, and turns the most-ignored accessibility requirement into a signature HUD moment.
proposals.approach: SmoothScroll.tsx: after lenis.scrollTo, run `if(!el.hasAttribute('tabindex')) el.setAttribute('tabindex','-1'); el.focus({preventScroll:true})`. This fixes the measured broken skip link and the nav focus hand-off. New FocusReticle.tsx, mounted in layout: listens for focusin/focusout and shows only when document.activeElement.matches(':focus-visible'). It positions a fixed 4-corner bracket box over the element's rect with transform, tracks scroll and resize with rAF while focused, snaps in 120 ms, and colours the corners with --accent so they follow the section palette. The native 2px outline stays, and `@media (forced-colors: active)` keeps it system-coloured. Skills.tsx gets the full ARIA tabs pattern: ids, aria-controls, role=tabpanel with aria-labelledby, roving tabindex, and ArrowLeft/Right/Home/End. Nav.tsx: the mobile overlay becomes role=dialog with aria-modal and aria-label='Menu'; on open, focus the first link and set `inert` on #main and the footer; on close, return focus to the burger. The 剣/杖 button gets aria-pressed. Preloader.tsx: inert page and a focused Skip button. Hero.tsx: the h1 gets one sr-only text node with the per-char spans aria-hidden. Fix the stats <dl> (axe 'definition-list', serious) by putting dt first and the note inside dd. Counter.tsx: sr-only final value.
proposals.risk: The reticle must not read as a replacement for the custom cursor the owner removed. It is :focus-visible only, hides on any pointer interaction, and never replaces the native outline. Roving tabindex turns the 3 Skills tab stops into 1, which is the intended pattern. inert is supported in all evergreen browsers.
proposals.mobile: Mostly benefits switch-access users and tablet users with external keyboards. The menu-as-dialog fix also stops VoiceOver from reading the page underneath the open menu.

proposals.title: Nothing breaks the spell: error boundaries, an honest contact form, and a summoning-failed 404
proposals.pitch: If a chunk fails to load (a flaky mobile network, an ad blocker, an old tab after a redeploy), the sigil quietly falls back to its SVG twin; the whole site no longer turns into 'Application error'. The contact form tells the truth: when mail delivery isn't wired up it says so and hands you a prefilled email, instead of claiming 'Message sent'. Dead links land on a 召喚失敗 'Summoning failed' page with a broken circle whose six glyphs lead back to the six sections.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero builds trust with sourced captions. This adds a matching honest-failure posture: the site never shows a fake success and never shows a framework error page.
proposals.approach: Add src/components/ui/Boundary.tsx (a small class error boundary) around <ManaCore> in Hero.tsx. Its fallback leaves MagicCircle visible because gpu stays false. Also catch the next/dynamic import so a rejected chunk resolves to a null component. Add src/app/error.tsx (themed 'The circle broke' with a Recast button calling reset()) and src/app/global-error.tsx. On ChunkLoadError, reload once behind a sessionStorage guard. Contact: route.ts returns {ok:true, delivered:false} when RESEND_API_KEY or CONTACT_TO_EMAIL is missing. Contact.tsx then shows 'Not delivered — open this in your mail app' with a mailto: link carrying a prefilled subject and body. Client-side validation mirrors the server rules (name at least 2 chars, email regex, message at least 10). Each field gets aria-invalid and aria-describedby, and focus moves to the first invalid field. Error text uses a new --danger token per theme: about 185 28 28 in light (at least 5:1 on the pink wash) and 248 113 113 in dark. not-found.tsx becomes '召喚失敗 · Summoning failed', using MagicCircle with one ring arc missing and an unclosed star (new props on MagicCircle.tsx), the requested path echoed in a HUD line, and the six nav glyphs on the hexagram as links back. With the heartbeat store, Telemetry stops claiming 'Section 01 Work' there. globals.css sets `color-scheme: light` or `color-scheme: dark` per data-theme so native controls, scrollbars and autofill match the dark default.
proposals.risk: Reload-on-ChunkLoadError needs its loop guard. The mailto fallback exposes nothing new, since the address is already on the page. Keep the 404 light, because bots receive it too.
proposals.mobile: Flaky mobile networks are exactly where chunk failures happen. Phones never load three.js, but their framer and page chunks can still fail, and the global boundary covers those. The --danger token fixes the error contrast on the light theme everywhere.

proposals.title: Budgets as code: the gate every other proposal must pass
proposals.pitch: Visitors never see this, but it decides the site. One `npm run audit` boots the production build and fails if an addition makes the site slower, jankier, less accessible or less honest than agreed. That lets WebGL stages, scroll choreography and a command palette all land without the phone experience regressing.
proposals.beatsCarbonZero: CarbonZero shows sourced numbers in its UI. This holds the portfolio to measured numbers on every change, so claims about speed and accessibility stay true.
proposals.approach: scripts/audit.mjs runs Playwright plus axe-core. axe-core is already in node_modules transitively; make it an explicit devDependency. The script starts `next start` on a free port, kills only its own process group, and takes the median of 3 runs. Gates, with today's value first: mobile profile 390x844, 4x CPU, 1.6 Mbps/150 ms. LCP 5404 ms, gate 2500 ms. CLS 0.0028, gate 0.05. Long tasks after FCP 2352 ms across 19 tasks, gate 600 ms total. First-load JS for '/' 191 KB gz, gate 200 KB gz. No WebGL chunk below 768px. Desktop lazy 3D 118 KB gz, gate 60 KB gz. Fonts about 253 KB across 7 files, gate 180 KB; self-subset Inter via next/font/local to drop the 85 KB latin-ext fetched for ₹ ō ū Ō. axe: zero serious or critical per section in both themes (today there is 1, the hero dl). Under reduced motion and 静: zero running infinite animations and zero rAF callbacks over 2 s. Keyboard: the skip link and nav links must move focus into their targets. Resilience: aborting any lazy chunk must not render 'Application error'. Honesty: /api/contact must never report delivered when no provider is configured. Palette parity between globals.css and palettes.ts. Rules handed to the other lenses: WebGL gets one context site-wide, DPR capped at 1.5 (ManaCore uses 1.75 with antialias), pauses off-screen and when hidden, falls back to the SVG on webglcontextlost, does its motion on the GPU (no per-frame CPU buffer uploads like ManaCore's 1,100-mote loop), uses time-based dt, re-renders its static frame on palette or theme change, and mounts only after LCP via requestIdleCallback. Drop the three dependency once the raw-WebGL2 stage the WebGL lens is prototyping replaces ManaCore, or port ManaCore itself to about 6 KB of raw WebGL2. Motion: no above-the-fold text SSR'd at opacity:0, scroll-linked effects use only transform and opacity, and every continuous loop registers with the shared ticker. Interaction: overlays and any ⌘K palette follow the dialog or combobox pattern with an inert background, focus return and lazy loading, and targets are at least 24px. Also replace the full-viewport `.noise` layer (z-9998, mix-blend-mode soft-light) with a pre-tinted low-alpha tile, or drop it in the lite and still tiers.
proposals.risk: SwiftShader lab numbers inflate GPU work (ManaCore init showed a 3.4 s long task here), so gate on main-thread and CPU metrics at 4x throttle and treat GPU timings as relative. Timing gates flake without medians. A gate that is too strict blocks good work, so start at today's values plus the targets above and tighten later.
proposals.mobile: Mobile is the gated profile. The phone budget (200 KB JS gz or less, no WebGL below 768px, no perpetual full-screen canvases) becomes enforced instead of remembered.
